tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

schema.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
schema.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). # Built-in browser

The built-in browser is a real browser pane inside the Claude desktop app, separate from the person's Chrome. Its tools are named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*` when the session itself runs inside the desktop app, and `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` when the session runs in the cloud (started from the web, a phone, or the desktop app) and is linked to the person's computer. The names after the prefix are the same either way, Claude uses whichever prefix is actually present, and this skill refers to the tools by the part after the prefix.

If the only built-in browser tool present is `enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser`, Claude calls it first: it turns the built-in browser on for this conversation, and the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` tools appear once it has run.

## What the person can see

The browser pane shares the desktop app's side panel with artifacts, documents, and file previews, and the panel shows one of them at a time. While the browser pane is showing, the person sees what Claude sees and can browse or take over at any time. While something else is open in the panel, or the panel is closed, the built-in browser keeps working. Claude does not tell the person that they missed it or could not see it, because Claude cannot tell what they were watching.

Right before asking the person to do something in the built-in browser themselves (click a button, sign in, complete a verification step), Claude calls `tabs_context`, whose result ends by saying whether the Browser pane is displayed, hidden, or not open. If the pane is not open, Claude opens the page first and checks again. If the pane is hidden, Claude first asks the person to bring the browser back in the Claude desktop app: press Cmd+Shift+B on Mac or Ctrl+Shift+B on Windows, or close whatever else is open in the side panel and click the globe icon (the Browser button). When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, Claude usually cannot tell whether the person is reading this conversation in the desktop app, on the claude.ai website or on a phone, and the shortcut and the globe icon work only in the desktop app, so before those steps Claude says that if they are not in the Claude desktop app on the computer whose browser Claude is using, they need to open this conversation there first. Claude then says what to do in the browser. Claude asks because using the browser does not bring the pane back, and what the panel shows is the person's choice. Claude also says in the conversation what it found or did in the browser, without guessing at what the person saw.

## Sign-ins persist, and they are the person's

The built-in browser keeps its own persistent profile, shared across the desktop app's sessions. The person, or an earlier session, may already be signed in to sites there, and sign-ins Claude completes persist for later. Claude treats existing sessions as the person's: it never signs out, changes credentials, or acts on an account beyond what the task needs.

## Tabs

The built-in browser has tabs. `preview_start` with a `url` opens an additional tab at that URL in one call and returns a `tabId`, leaving existing tabs untouched, so Claude prefers it over `tabs_create` followed by `navigate` when the destination is already known. `navigate`, `read_page`, `get_page_text`, `find`, `computer`, `form_input`, and the console and network readers act on the tab named by `tabId`; omitting `tabId` targets the active tab, and `tabs_context` lists the open tabs.

## Loading via ToolSearch

Claude loads the built-in browser tools in bulk, not one-by-one: if they are in the deferred list, Claude loads them all in a single ToolSearch call whose query is their full name prefix, for example `{ query: "mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__", max_results: 64 }`.

## Reading pages

Claude prefers `get_page_text` and `read_page` over screenshots for reading, because they return the page's actual text and structure rather than pixels of the visible viewport. `computer` with action "screenshot" is for when the visual layout is the point or the person asks to see the page.

## Site approvals, blocked sites, and request_access

Depending on the person's approval settings, the person may be asked to approve a site before Claude acts on it, and some sites are blocked outright. Claude waits for a pending approval rather than working around it. If a page is refused or an approval is declined, Claude tells the person and moves on rather than retrying.

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, approvals can be answered from any of the person's devices and may take a moment to arrive, and the session may also have a `request_access` tool. If a browser tool answers that the site is not allowed yet and `request_access` is present, Claude calls it with that site's URL and scope "once" (or "site" when the task will keep using that site), waits for the person's answer, and then retries the original tool. Without `request_access`, a refused site is handled as above: Claude tells the person and moves on.

## What the built-in browser cannot open

The built-in browser cannot open `file://` URLs or `localhost` servers that Claude starts itself, because those run where Claude's shell runs, which is not where the browser pane runs. To show the person HTML that Claude generated, Claude uses an artifact instead.

## When the built-in browser cannot be reached

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, the pane runs in the Claude desktop app on the person's computer while Claude runs elsewhere, so it is reachable only while that app is open and online. If those tool calls cannot reach the desktop app (connection errors or no response), Claude tells the person the built-in browser looks offline on their computer rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

# Flowline PowerCenter Demo — Jaffle Shop

A single Informatica PowerCenter repository export (`FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml`) that reimplements the dbt [Jaffle Shop](https://github.com/dbt-labs/jaffle-shop) demo project as a PowerCenter pipeline. Used for demo purposes only.

## Contents

The export contains one repository (`REPO_Jaffleshop`) and folder (`FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP`) targeting Oracle, with:

- **Sources** — `RAW_*` tables (customers, orders, items, products, supplies, stores) plus staged `STG_*` tables.
- **Targets** — staging tables (`STG_*`), core marts (`CUSTOMERS`, `ORDERS`, `ORDER_ITEMS`, `PRODUCTS`, `SUPPLIES`), and enriched marts (`CUSTOMER_360`, `ORDER_FINANCIALS`, `ORDER_ITEM_ENRICHED`, `PRODUCT_DAILY_PERFORMANCE`, `STORE_DAILY_KPIS`).
- **Mappings** — `m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL`, `m_FL_JS_MARTS_CORE`, `m_FL_JS_MARTS_ENRICHED`.
- **Workflow** — `wf_FL_JAFFLESHOP_DEMO`, running the three mappings via sessions `s_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL`, `s_FL_JS_MARTS_CORE`, `s_FL_JS_MARTS_ENRICHED`.

The pipeline flows RAW → staging → core marts → enriched marts.

## Usage

Import `FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml` into a PowerCenter repository via the Repository Manager or `pmrep`.

# Flowline PowerCenter Demo — Jaffle Shop

A single Informatica PowerCenter repository export (`FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml`) that reimplements the dbt [Jaffle Shop](https://github.com/dbt-labs/jaffle-shop) demo project as a PowerCenter pipeline. Used for demo purposes only.

## Contents

The export contains one repository (`REPO_Jaffleshop`) and folder (`FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP`) targeting Oracle, with:

- **Sources** — `RAW_*` tables (customers, orders, items, products, supplies, stores) plus staged `STG_*` tables.
- **Targets** — staging tables (`STG_*`), core marts (`CUSTOMERS`, `ORDERS`, `ORDER_ITEMS`, `PRODUCTS`, `SUPPLIES`), and enriched marts (`CUSTOMER_360`, `ORDER_FINANCIALS`, `ORDER_ITEM_ENRICHED`, `PRODUCT_DAILY_PERFORMANCE`, `STORE_DAILY_KPIS`).
- **Mappings** — `m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL`, `m_FL_JS_MARTS_CORE`, `m_FL_JS_MARTS_ENRICHED`.
- **Workflow** — `wf_FL_JAFFLESHOP_DEMO`, running the three mappings via sessions `s_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL`, `s_FL_JS_MARTS_CORE`, `s_FL_JS_MARTS_ENRICHED`.

The pipeline flows RAW → staging → core marts → enriched marts.

## Usage

Import `FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml` into a PowerCenter repository via the Repository Manager or `pmrep`.
    4701 FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml
  728727 FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml

---
Assignment
Take-home exercise: Informatica PowerCenter to dbt converter

This exercise is part of our interview process for the Product Engineer role. Plan for about four hours of work. You have one week from receipt to return it.

What we are asking

Build a small tool that converts an Informatica PowerCenter mapping into an equivalent dbt model. We have attached one sample PowerCenter mapping file in XML to work from. Download the demo XML workflow here: https://github.com/infinitelambda/flowline-pwc-demo

The mapping mirrors the dbt jaffle shop demo project, which is public. You can use that project as a reference target: run it, look at its models, and check your converter's output against it. Build a converter that derives the dbt model from the XML. Do not hard-code the jaffle shop output, because we are assessing the conversion logic, not the final SQL.

You are not expected to know either tool in advance. Part of what we want to see is how you get up to speed on an unfamiliar system, so the reading below is enough to start.

Background

Informatica PowerCenter is an ETL tool. A mapping describes how data moves from source tables to target tables through a chain of transformations (filters, joins, lookups, aggregations, and so on). Mappings can be exported as XML, which is the format we have given you.

Mappings overview: https://docs.informatica.com/data-integration/powercenter/10-5/designer-guide/mappings/mappings-overview.html

Transformation guide: https://docs.informatica.com/data-integration/powercenter/10-5/transformation-guide/preface.html

dbt transforms data already in a warehouse using SQL. A dbt model is a single SQL select statement in a .sql file that dbt turns into a table or view. Models can reference each other, and you can attach tests and documentation.

What is dbt: https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/introduction

About dbt models: https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/models

SQL models: https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/sql-models

Quickstart guides: https://docs.getdbt.com/guides

Jaffle shop reference project (runs locally with DuckDB in about a minute): https://github.com/dbt-labs/jaffle_shop_duckdb

The task

Read the sample PowerCenter XML and work out what the mapping does.

Build a converter, in any language you choose, that reads a PowerCenter mapping XML and produces an equivalent dbt model.

Include tests. You can check your output against the jaffle shop reference project.

Handle what you reasonably can in the time. We care more about how you reason about the problem than about full coverage.

Using coding agents

We expect you to use coding agents such as Claude Code or Cursor. This is how the team works day to day, and we want to see how you use them. If you do not have access to a tool, tell us and we may be able to provide access or refund you for your spend.

What to submit

A GitHub repository (public, or private with access granted to [GitHub handles]) or a zipped folder, with a short README that covers:

How to run it.

What you assumed, and what you chose not to handle.

Where the converter is most likely to produce wrong output.

Where a coding agent got something wrong, and how you caught it.

The prompts you gave the coding agent, starting with your initial prompt. If your tool can export the full agent conversation, include it as a file in the repository.

A short outline of the process you followed with the agent to build the solution.

What we are looking for

You understand the code you submit and can explain any part of it.

Sensible handling of the conversion, with a clear view of where it breaks.

Clear reasoning in the README.

Logistics

Effort: about 04 hours. Please do not over-invest.

Deadline: one week from receipt.

Questions: contact [recruiter name removed] @ [recruiter email removed]

content.text:
# PowerCenter → dbt: the problem in 5 minutes

**In one sentence:** PowerCenter is an older ETL tool where people build data pipelines by drawing boxes and wires, and it can save that drawing as XML. dbt does the same job with plain SQL files. You're building a tool that reads the XML and writes the dbt SQL.

All line numbers below point to [FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml](https://github.com/infinitelambda/flowline-pwc-demo/blob/main/FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml) (4,701 lines). On GitHub, add `#L106` to the URL to jump to a line.

## 1. The input: what's inside the XML

The file holds four kinds of things:

- **Sources** are the raw tables data comes from. Example: `RAW_ORDERS` with columns `ID`, `CUSTOMER`, `ORDERED_AT`, `SUBTOTAL`… (L26–34).
- **Targets** are the tables the pipeline writes to. Example: `STG_ORDERS` (L67–78).
- **Mappings** hold the actual logic, and there are 3: `m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL` (L90), `m_FL_JS_MARTS_ENRICHED` (L1210) and `m_FL_JS_MARTS_CORE` (L3107). Each one has:
  - **Transformations**, the boxes. There are 98: Source Qualifier 28, Expression 25, Joiner 16, Sorter 15, Aggregator 9, Router 2, Union 2, Filter 1.
  - **Connectors**, the wires. Each one connects one column to one column. Example, L643: `SQ_RAW_ORDERS.ID → EXP_ORDERS.ID`.
- **Workflow and sessions** set the run order: staging → core → enriched (L4623–4625). The rest is mostly runtime settings like connections and logs, which don't matter for SQL.

A few real boxes, so you can see the logic language:

| Box type | Line | What it says | SQL idea |
|---|---|---|---|
| Expression | L111 | `SUBTOTAL = SUBTOTAL_IN/100` | a computed column |
| Filter | L2385 | `NOT ISNULL(LOCATION_ID)` | `WHERE` |
| Joiner | L488 | `SKU1 = SKU`, "Normal Join" | `JOIN … ON` |
| Aggregator | L1443 | `SUM(SUPPLY_COST)` | `GROUP BY` |
| Router | L276 | `REGION = 'APAC'` | splits rows into groups |

## 2. The output: what we produce

The output is a small dbt project: one `.sql` file per target table, plus a `sources.yml` that lists the raw tables. Each `.sql` file is just one `SELECT`.

**Example.** The XML box `EXP_ORDERS` (L106–125), with attributes trimmed:

```xml
<TRANSFORMFIELD NAME="ORDER_ID"       EXPRESSION="ID"/>
<TRANSFORMFIELD NAME="CUSTOMER_ID"    EXPRESSION="CUSTOMER"/>
<TRANSFORMFIELD NAME="ORDERED_AT_DAY" EXPRESSION="TO_DATE(TO_CHAR(ORDERED_AT,'DD-MM-YY'),'DD-MM-YY')"/>
<TRANSFORMFIELD NAME="SUBTOTAL"       EXPRESSION="SUBTOTAL_IN/100"/>
```

should become something like `models/staging/stg_orders.sql`:

```sql
with source as (
    select * from {{ source('raw', 'raw_orders') }}
),
exp_orders as (
    select
        id                            as order_id,
        customer                      as customer_id,
        date_trunc('day', ordered_at) as ordered_at_day,
        subtotal / 100                as subtotal
    from source
)
select * from exp_orders
```

The reference project's [stg_orders.sql](https://github.com/dbt-labs/jaffle-shop/blob/main/models/staging/stg_orders.sql#L14-L27) does almost exactly this, so you can compare against it.

## 3. What we're building, and how we'd know it's right

**The converter, in 5 steps:**
1. **Parse:** read the XML into objects (sources, targets, boxes, wires).
2. **Graph:** the boxes become nodes and the connectors become edges.
3. **Walk:** for each target, follow the wires back to its sources.
4. **Translate:** turn each box into one SQL step (a CTE), and translate Informatica's own functions into SQL. For example, `IIF` becomes `CASE WHEN` and `ISNULL(x)` becomes `x IS NULL`. There are 389 expressions to handle.
5. **Write:** produce the `.sql` files and `sources.yml`.

**Where it gets hard:**
- **Follow the wires, not the names.** At L608 and L611, `SUBTOTAL` (dollars) is wired into the `SUBTOTAL_CENTS` column, and the reverse. A converter that matches by name will hide this. A faithful one copies it, and we call it out.
- **Some boxes have no direct SQL equivalent.** Sorters (15) mean nothing in a table. A "variable port" that remembers the previous row (L3588–3590, a running order number per customer) needs a window function like `row_number()`. "Master Outer Join" (L1350) is easy to flip the wrong way.

**How we know the output is right, in 3 layers:**
1. **Unit tests:** small XML piece in, expected SQL out, one test per box type and function.
2. **It compiles:** `dbt compile` passes and the SQL runs in DuckDB.
3. **It matches the reference data:** load the jaffle shop seed data, run our models and the reference models, and compare row counts and values.

**⚠️ One mismatch to know early:**
- The brief links [jaffle_shop_duckdb](https://github.com/dbt-labs/jaffle_shop_duckdb), the old version with 3 tables (customers, orders, payments).
- The XML actually mirrors the newer [jaffle-shop](https://github.com/dbt-labs/jaffle-shop), with 6 raw tables (customers, orders, items, products, supplies, stores). The demo repo's README links that one.
- jaffle-shop is set up for cloud warehouses, so we'd have to get it running on DuckDB ourselves.
- The 5 "enriched" targets (`CUSTOMER_360`, `STORE_DAILY_KPIS`, …) have no reference at all. Those can only be checked with our own tests.

## 4. What to submit

- [ ] A GitHub repo (public, or private with access granted) or a zip
- [ ] Converter code in any language, plus tests
- [ ] README: how to run it
- [ ] README: what you assumed and what you chose not to handle
- [ ] README: where the converter is most likely to be wrong
- [ ] README: where the coding agent got something wrong, and how you caught it
- [ ] README: your prompts, starting with the first one. This message counts. Include the exported conversation as a file.
- [ ] README: a short outline of your process with the agent
- [ ] Be ready to explain any line. Budget about 4 hours, due 1 week after you received it.

The brief says to give access to "[GitHub handles]" but never fills them in. If you go with a private repo, ask [recruiter name removed] which handles to add.

"""Classify every EXPRESSION attribute in a PowerCenter XML export.

Usage: python3 -I count_expr.py <path-to-xml>
"""
import re
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from collections import Counter

IDENT = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*$")

path = sys.argv[1]
root = ET.parse(path).getroot()

raw_lines = sum(1 for line in open(path, encoding="cp1252") if 'EXPRESSION ="' in line)
print(f"raw lines containing 'EXPRESSION =\"': {raw_lines}")

# Where do EXPRESSION attributes live?
holders = Counter(el.tag for el in root.iter() if "EXPRESSION" in el.attrib)
print("elements carrying EXPRESSION:", dict(holders))

cats = Counter()
by_type = {}
logic_by_porttype = Counter()
for tr in root.iter("TRANSFORMATION"):
    ttype = tr.get("TYPE")
    for f in tr.iter("TRANSFORMFIELD"):
        expr = f.get("EXPRESSION")
        if expr is None:
            continue
        e = expr.strip()
        name = f.get("NAME")
        if e == "":
            cat = "empty"
        elif e == name:
            cat = "same-name pass-through"
        elif IDENT.match(e):
            cat = "rename (bare column)"
        else:
            cat = "real logic"
            logic_by_porttype[f.get("PORTTYPE")] += 1
        cats[cat] += 1
        by_type.setdefault(ttype, Counter())[cat] += 1

print("\nTRANSFORMFIELD expressions:")
for k, v in cats.most_common():
    print(f"  {k:28s} {v}")
print(f"  {'TOTAL':28s} {sum(cats.values())}")

print("\nBy transformation type:")
for t, c in sorted(by_type.items()):
    print(f"  {t:24s} {dict(c)}")

print("\nReal-logic ports by PORTTYPE:", dict(logic_by_porttype))

groups = [g for g in root.iter("GROUP") if g.get("EXPRESSION")]
print(f"\nRouter GROUP conditions: {len(groups)}")

11:> This project is geared towards folks learning dbt Cloud with a cloud warehouse. If you're brand new to dbt, we recommend starting with the [dbt Learn](https://learn.getdbt.com/) platform. It's a free, interactive way to learn dbt, and it's a great way to get started if you're new to the tool. If you just want to try dbt locally as quickly as possible without setting up a data warehouse check out [`jaffle_shop_duckdb`](https://github.com/dbt-labs/jaffle_shop_duckdb).
46:- A data warehouse (BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Databricks, or Postgres) with adequate permissions to create a fresh database for this project and run dbt in it
64:1. Create a logical database in your data warehouse for the Jaffle Shop project. We recommend using the name `jaffle_shop` for consistency with the project. This looks different on different platforms (for instance on BigQuery this constitutes creating a new _project_, on Snowflake this is achieved via `create database jaffle_shop;`, and if you're running Postgres locally you can probably skip this). If you're not sure how to do this, we recommend checking out the [Quickstart Guide for your data platform in the dbt Docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/guides).
76:- dbt Cloud connected to your warehouse
78:- dbt Cloud and the codebase pointed at a fresh database or project in your warehouse to work in
93:   python3 -m pip install dbt
96:3. [Set up a `profiles.yml`](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/core/connect-data-platform/connection-profiles#connecting-to-your-warehouse-using-the-command-line) with your warehouse connection details, and add a top-level `profile` key to `dbt_project.yml` pointing at it, e.g. `profile: my-profile-name`.
108:- **Load the data via S3**. If you'd prefer a larger dataset (6 years instead of 1), and are working via the dbt Cloud IDE and your platform's web interface, you can also copy the data from a public S3 bucket to your warehouse into a schema called `raw` in your `jaffle_shop` database. [This is discussed here](#-load-the-data-from-s3).
110:- **Generate a larger dataset on the command line**. If you're working with the dbt CLI locally and comfortable with command line basics, you can generate as many years of data as you'd like (up to 10) to load into your warehouse. [This is discussed here](#-generate-via-jafgen-and-seed-the-data-with-dbt-core).
122:- Synthetic data loaded into your warehouse
149:4. Fill out the credentials with your warehouse connection details, in real production you'll want to make a Service Account or similar and only give access to the production schema to that user, so that only dbt Cloud Jobs can build into production. For this demo project, it's okay to just use your account credentials.
178:6. This will kick off a Job to build your project in the `Prod` Environment, which will build into the `prod` schema in your warehouse.
180:7. Go check out the `prod` schema in your `jaffle_shop` database on your warehouse, you should see the project's models built there!
206:To load the data from S3, consult the [dbt Documentation's Quickstart Guides](https://docs.getdbt.com/guides) for your data platform to see how to copy data from an S3 bucket to your warehouse. The S3 bucket URIs of the tables you want to copy into your `raw` schema are:
219:You'll need to be working on the command line for this option. If you're more comfortable working via web apps, the above method is the path you'll need. [`jafgen`](https://github.com/dbt-labs/jaffle-shop-generator) is a simple tool for generating synthetic Jaffle Shop data that is maintained on a volunteer-basis by dbt Labs employees. This project is more interesting with a larger dataset generated and uploaded to your warehouse. 6 years is a nice amount to fully observe trends like growth, seasonality, and buyer personas that exist in the data. Uploading this amount of data requires a few extra steps, but we'll walk you through them. If you have a preferred way of loading CSVs into your warehouse or an S3 bucket, that will also work just fine, the generated data is just CSV files.
226:2. [Add a profile for your warehouse connection in this file](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/core/connect-data-platform/connection-profiles#connecting-to-your-warehouse-using-the-command-line) and add this configuration to your `dbt_project.yml` file as a top-level key called `profile` e.g. `profile: my-profile-name`.
231:3. Create a new virtual environment in your project (I like to call mine `.venv`) and activate it, then install the project's dependencies in it. This will install the `jafgen` tool which you can use to generate the larger datasets. Then install dbt. We install dbt temporarily because by connecting directly to your warehouse, it can upload larger file sizes than the dbt Cloud server[^1]. You can do this manually or with `task`:
236:python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt
237:python3 -m pip install dbt
===
version: "3"

silent: true

vars:
  YEARS: 6

tasks:
  venv:
    cmds:
      - python3 -m venv .venv

  install:
    cmds:
      - source .venv/bin/activate && python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip --progress-bar off > /dev/null
      - source .venv/bin/activate && python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt --progress-bar off > /dev/null
      - source .venv/bin/activate && python3 -m pip install dbt > /dev/null

  gen:
    cmds:
      - source .venv/bin/activate && jafgen {{.YEARS}} && rm -rf seeds/jaffle-data && mv jaffle-data seeds

  seed:
    cmds:
      - >
        source .venv/bin/activate && dbt seed --full-refresh --vars '{"load_source_data": true}'

  clean:
    cmds:
      - rm -rf jaffle-data
      - source .venv/bin/activate && python3 -m pip uninstall dbt -y

  load:
    cmds:
      - task: venv
      - task: install
      - task: gen
      - task: seed
      - task: clean

content.content: Launching skill: artifact-diagramming

content.text:
Draw as the engineer who has to live with the decision, not as a decorator: a diagram earns its place when it lets a cold reader see a mechanism they would otherwise have to assemble from prose - where data flows, which components talk, what changes between two options, what state a request moves through. If a sentence says it faster, write the sentence.

## What to draw

**Depict the mechanism, not its name.** A box labeled "cache" says less than the prose; the path a request takes through it, the two stores it sits between, and the arrow that disappears when the cache is removed say what the words can't. Show the parts that the argument hinges on - the boundary being crossed, the hop being added, the data that moves - and leave out the parts that don't.

**Comparing options?** Draw the difference. Two architectures side by side, a before and an after, the one edge that each option adds or removes - the reader should be able to point at what they are choosing between. A separate labeled box per option, with nothing connecting them to the system, is not a comparison; it is a restated option list.

**Match complexity to the stakes.** A one-hop question is a three-box diagram; a migration that reroutes writes through a queue needs the queue, the writer, the reader, and the ordering arrow. Draw as much as the decision actually turns on - no forced minimalism, no inventory of the whole system either.

**Label the arrows.** An unlabeled arrow is "related somehow"; `writes`, `invalidates`, `polls every 30s` is information. A legend is only worth it when the same encoding (dashed, colored, doubled) repeats; otherwise put the meaning on the mark itself.

## Inline SVG mechanics

These mechanics apply where the page renders inline SVG natively (HTML pages); a markdown-rendered page draws its diagrams in whatever fence that lane's renderer supports, and the skill that owns the lane says which. An artifact made from an Artifact type draws its diagrams the way the type's instructions, and the reference pages they name, say to; these mechanics apply there only where those say nothing about diagrams. Hand-author inline `<svg>` with native shapes (`rect`, `circle`, `line`, `polyline`, `path`) and `<text>` - no libraries, no runtime, no external images.

- **Size by `viewBox`.** Set `viewBox="0 0 W H"` and let CSS scale it (`max-width: 100%; height: auto`); choose W and H for the content, not a preset. Wide flows read left-to-right; layered stacks read top-to-bottom.
- **Theme with `currentColor`.** Strokes, text, and arrowheads in `currentColor` inherit the page's foreground in light and dark themes alike; reserve a literal hue for the one element that carries meaning (the option leaned toward, the hop under discussion), and make sure it reads on both grounds.
- **Arrowheads are markers or polygons.** A `<defs><marker>` referenced by `marker-end="url(#arrow)"` (fragment-internal id) or a small `<polygon>` at the line's end - never an image.
- **Keep text legible.** Roughly 11-13px at the drawn scale, `text-anchor` for alignment, short labels (a word or three); explanatory sentences belong in the caption below the figure, not in the drawing.
- **Align to a grid.** Shared baselines and even gaps are most of what makes a hand diagram read as deliberate; eyeballed offsets read as noise.
- **One figure, one claim.** Wrap the `<svg>` in `<figure>` with a `<figcaption>` that states what the picture shows, and give the `<svg>` `role="img"` plus an `aria-label` carrying the same claim for readers who cannot see it.
- **Stay self-contained.** No `<script>`, `<style>`, or `<foreignObject>` inside the SVG; gradients, patterns, and `<use>` reference ids in the same fragment (`href="#id"`). Long decorative path data is a sign the drawing wants a real graphics tool - simplify instead.

"""Per-mapping facts from a PowerCenter XML export (no attribute values from tasks are printed).

Usage: python3 -I mapping_facts.py <path-to-xml>
"""
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from collections import Counter

root = ET.parse(sys.argv[1]).getroot()

for m in root.iter("MAPPING"):
    name = m.get("NAME")
    inst = m.findall("INSTANCE")
    srcs = sorted(i.get("NAME") for i in inst if i.get("TYPE") == "SOURCE")
    tgts = sorted(i.get("NAME") for i in inst if i.get("TYPE") == "TARGET")
    types = Counter(t.get("TYPE") for t in m.findall("TRANSFORMATION"))
    conns = len(m.findall("CONNECTOR"))
    print(f"\n{name}: {sum(types.values())} transformations, {conns} connectors")
    print("  sources:", srcs)
    print("  targets:", tgts)
    print("  types:", dict(types))
    for t in m.findall("TRANSFORMATION"):
        attrs = {a.get("NAME"): a.get("VALUE") for a in t.findall("TABLEATTRIBUTE")}
        if t.get("TYPE") == "Sorter" and attrs.get("Distinct") == "YES":
            print("  sorter with Distinct=YES:", t.get("NAME"))
        if t.get("TYPE") == "Joiner":
            print(f"  joiner {t.get('NAME')}: {attrs.get('Join Type')}")
        if t.get("TYPE") == "Source Qualifier":
            for k in ("Sql Query", "Source Filter", "User Defined Join"):
                if attrs.get(k):
                    print(f"  SQ {t.get('NAME')} has {k}")
            if attrs.get("Select Distinct") == "YES":
                print(f"  SQ {t.get('NAME')} Select Distinct=YES")

print("\nTotals:",
      "SOURCE", len(root.findall(".//SOURCE")),
      "TARGET", len(root.findall(".//TARGET")),
      "TRANSFORMATION", len(root.findall(".//TRANSFORMATION")),
      "CONNECTOR", len(root.findall(".//CONNECTOR")),
      "MAPPLET", len(root.findall(".//MAPPLET")))

"""Extract the RAW_ORDERS -> STG_ORDERS slice of the demo XML into docs/assets/example-data.js.

Every line number in the output is read from the file, never typed by hand.
The workflow command task's VALUEPAIR line (it holds a credential) is never read into the output,
and a final guard fails the run if any token of that value leaks into the generated file.

Usage: python3 -I build_example_data.py <xml> <out.js>
"""
import html
import json
import re
import sys

xml_path, out_path = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
raw = open(xml_path, encoding="cp1252").read().split("\n")
LINES = {i + 1: t for i, t in enumerate(raw)}

TAG = re.compile(r"^\s*<(/?)([A-Z]+)\b(.*?)(/?)>\s*$")
ATTR = re.compile(r'([A-Z_]+) ="([^"]*)"')


def parse(n):
    m = TAG.match(LINES[n])
    if not m:
        return None
    closing, tag, rest, selfclose = m.groups()
    attrs = {k: html.unescape(v) for k, v in ATTR.findall(rest)}
    return {"n": n, "close": bool(closing), "tag": tag, "attrs": attrs, "self": bool(selfclose)}


def show(p, keep):
    """Render a parsed line with only the attributes in `keep` (in that order)."""
    if p["close"]:
        return "</%s>" % p["tag"]
    parts = ['%s="%s"' % (k, p["attrs"][k]) for k in keep if k in p["attrs"]]
    return "<%s %s%s>" % (p["tag"], " ".join(parts), "/" if p["self"] else "")


def find(tag, name, lo=1, hi=None):
    hi = hi or len(LINES)
    for n in range(lo, hi + 1):
        p = parse(n)
        if p and not p["close"] and p["tag"] == tag and p["attrs"].get("NAME") == name:
            return n
    raise SystemExit("not found: %s %s" % (tag, name))


def block(start):
    """Lines from an opening tag to its matching closing tag (same tag name)."""
    tag = parse(start)["tag"]
    n = start
    while True:
        n += 1
        p = parse(n)
        if p and p["close"] and p["tag"] == tag:
            return list(range(start, n + 1))


KEEP = {
    "SOURCE": ["NAME", "OWNERNAME", "DATABASETYPE"],
    "SOURCEFIELD": ["NAME", "DATATYPE"],
    "TARGET": ["NAME", "DATABASETYPE"],
    "TARGETFIELD": ["NAME", "DATATYPE"],
    "TRANSFORMATION": ["NAME", "TYPE"],
    "TRANSFORMFIELD": ["NAME", "EXPRESSION", "PORTTYPE", "ISSORTKEY"],
    "TABLEATTRIBUTE": ["NAME", "VALUE"],
    "CONNECTOR": ["FROMINSTANCE", "FROMFIELD", "TOINSTANCE", "TOFIELD"],
    "INSTANCE": ["NAME", "TRANSFORMATION_NAME", "TYPE"],
    "SESSION": ["NAME", "MAPPINGNAME"],
    "SESSTRANSFORMATIONINST": ["SINSTANCENAME", "TRANSFORMATIONTYPE"],
    "SESSIONEXTENSION": ["NAME", "SINSTANCENAME", "TYPE"],
    "CONNECTIONREFERENCE": ["CONNECTIONNAME", "CONNECTIONTYPE"],
    "ATTRIBUTE": ["NAME", "VALUE"],
    "WORKFLOW": ["NAME"],
    "SCHEDULEINFO": ["SCHEDULETYPE"],
    "TASK": ["NAME", "TYPE"],
    "TASKINSTANCE": ["NAME", "TASKTYPE"],
    "WORKFLOWLINK": ["FROMTASK", "TOTASK"],
}
SHOW_TABLEATTR = {"Sql Query", "Source Filter", "User Defined Join", "Select Distinct", "Distinct"}


def render(ns):
    """Render line numbers as [n, text] rows, inserting an elision row where lines are skipped."""
    rows, prev = [], None
    for n in ns:
        if "VALUEPAIR" in LINES[n]:
            raise SystemExit("refusing to render a VALUEPAIR line")
        p = parse(n)
        if prev is not None and n != prev + 1:
            rows.append([None, "…"])
        keep = KEEP.get(p["tag"], ["NAME"])
        a = dict(p["attrs"])
        if p["tag"] == "TRANSFORMFIELD" and a.get("ISSORTKEY") != "YES":
            p["attrs"].pop("ISSORTKEY", None)
        rows.append([n, show(p, keep)])
        prev = n
    return rows


# ---------------- locate the slice ----------------
MAP_START = find("MAPPING", "m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL")
MAP_LINES = block(MAP_START)
MAP_END = MAP_LINES[-1]

SLICE = ["RAW_ORDERS", "SQ_RAW_ORDERS", "EXP_ORDERS", "SRT_ORDERS", "STG_ORDERS"]
starts = {
    "RAW_ORDERS": find("SOURCE", "RAW_ORDERS"),
    "SQ_RAW_ORDERS": find("TRANSFORMATION", "SQ_RAW_ORDERS", MAP_START, MAP_END),
    "EXP_ORDERS": find("TRANSFORMATION", "EXP_ORDERS", MAP_START, MAP_END),
    "SRT_ORDERS": find("TRANSFORMATION", "SRT_ORDERS", MAP_START, MAP_END),
    "STG_ORDERS": find("TARGET", "STG_ORDERS"),
}

connectors, instances = [], {}
for n in MAP_LINES:
    p = parse(n)
    if not p or p["close"]:
        continue
    if p["tag"] == "CONNECTOR":
        a = p["attrs"]
        if a["FROMINSTANCE"] in SLICE and a["TOINSTANCE"] in SLICE:
            connectors.append((n, a))
    if p["tag"] == "INSTANCE" and p["attrs"].get("NAME") in SLICE:
        instances[p["attrs"]["NAME"]] = n

nodes = []
for name in SLICE:
    ns = block(starts[name])
    keep_ns = []
    for n in ns:
        p = parse(n)
        if p["tag"] == "TABLEATTRIBUTE" and p["attrs"].get("NAME") not in SHOW_TABLEATTR:
            continue
        keep_ns.append(n)
    wires_in = sorted(n for n, a in connectors if a["TOINSTANCE"] == name)
    nodes.append({
        "id": name,
        "type": parse(starts[name])["attrs"].get("TYPE") or parse(starts[name])["tag"].title(),
        "start": ns[0], "end": ns[-1],
        "instanceLine": instances.get(name),
        "lines": render(keep_ns),
        "wiresIn": render(wires_in),
    })

# ---------------- session + workflow ----------------
SESSION_START = find("SESSION", "s_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL")
session_ns = [SESSION_START]
sess_block = block(SESSION_START)
for n in sess_block:
    p = parse(n)
    if not p or p["close"]:
        continue
    if p["tag"] == "SESSTRANSFORMATIONINST" and p["attrs"].get("SINSTANCENAME") in SLICE:
        session_ns.append(n)
writer = None
for n in sess_block:
    p = parse(n)
    if p and not p["close"] and p["tag"] == "SESSIONEXTENSION" and p["attrs"].get("SINSTANCENAME") == "STG_ORDERS" \
            and p["attrs"].get("TYPE") == "WRITER":
        writer = n
for n in block(writer):
    p = parse(n)
    if p["tag"] in ("SESSIONEXTENSION", "CONNECTIONREFERENCE"):
        session_ns.append(n)
    elif p["tag"] == "ATTRIBUTE" and p["attrs"].get("NAME") in {"Target load type", "Insert", "Truncate target table option"}:
        session_ns.append(n)
for n in sess_block:
    p = parse(n)
    if p and p["tag"] == "ATTRIBUTE" and p["attrs"].get("NAME") == "Treat source rows as":
        session_ns.append(n)
session_ns = sorted(set(session_ns))

WF_START = find("WORKFLOW", "wf_FL_JAFFLESHOP_DEMO")
wf_ns = [WF_START]
for n in block(WF_START):
    if "VALUEPAIR" in LINES[n]:
        continue
    p = parse(n)
    if not p or p["close"]:
        continue
    if p["tag"] in ("SCHEDULEINFO", "WORKFLOWLINK", "TASKINSTANCE") or (p["tag"] == "TASK" and p["attrs"].get("TYPE") == "Command"):
        wf_ns.append(n)
wf_ns = sorted(set(wf_ns))
links = [parse(n)["attrs"] for n in wf_ns if parse(n)["tag"] == "WORKFLOWLINK"]

# ---------------- column lineage ----------------
port_line = {}  # (instance, port) -> line of TRANSFORMFIELD / SOURCEFIELD / TARGETFIELD
port_expr = {}
port_type = {}
for name in SLICE:
    for n in block(starts[name]):
        p = parse(n)
        if p["tag"] in ("TRANSFORMFIELD", "SOURCEFIELD", "TARGETFIELD"):
            port_line[(name, p["attrs"]["NAME"])] = n
            port_type[(name, p["attrs"]["NAME"])] = p["attrs"].get("PORTTYPE") or p["attrs"].get("DATATYPE")
            if "EXPRESSION" in p["attrs"]:
                port_expr[(name, p["attrs"]["NAME"])] = p["attrs"]["EXPRESSION"]

incoming = {(a["TOINSTANCE"], a["TOFIELD"]): (n, a) for n, a in connectors}
target_cols = [parse(n)["attrs"]["NAME"] for n in block(starts["STG_ORDERS"]) if parse(n)["tag"] == "TARGETFIELD"]
QUOTED = re.compile(r"'[^']*'")
IDENT = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*")


def lineage(inst, port, out, depth=0):
    if depth > 20:
        raise SystemExit("lineage too deep")
    key = (inst, port)
    if inst == "RAW_ORDERS":
        out.append({"n": port_line[key], "text": "%s.%s" % (inst, port), "kind": "PC Source column"})
        return
    expr = port_expr.get(key)
    ptype = port_type.get(key, "")
    if expr is not None and ptype in ("OUTPUT", "LOCAL VARIABLE") and inst != "STG_ORDERS":
        out.append({"n": port_line[key], "text": "%s.%s = %s" % (inst, port, expr), "kind": "port expression"})
        names = set(IDENT.findall(QUOTED.sub("", expr)))
        for nm in sorted(names):
            if (inst, nm) in port_type and port_type[(inst, nm)] in ("INPUT", "INPUT/OUTPUT"):
                lineage(inst, nm, out, depth + 1)
        return
    n, a = incoming[key]
    out.append({"n": n, "text": "%s.%s ← %s.%s" % (inst, port, a["FROMINSTANCE"], a["FROMFIELD"]), "kind": "connector"})
    lineage(a["FROMINSTANCE"], a["FROMFIELD"], out, depth + 1)


lin, flags = {}, []
for col in target_cols:
    chain = []
    lineage("STG_ORDERS", col, chain)
    n, a = incoming[("STG_ORDERS", col)]
    crossed = a["FROMFIELD"] != col and a["FROMFIELD"] in target_cols
    if crossed:
        chain[0]["flag"] = True
        flags.append({"n": n, "column": col, "from": "%s.%s" % (a["FROMINSTANCE"], a["FROMFIELD"])})
    lin[col] = chain

data = {
    "xmlFile": "FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml",
    "mapping": {"name": "m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL", "start": MAP_START, "end": MAP_END},
    "nodes": nodes,
    "wireCounts": [{"from": a, "to": b, "count": sum(1 for _, c in connectors if c["FROMINSTANCE"] == a and c["TOINSTANCE"] == b)}
                   for a, b in zip(SLICE, SLICE[1:])],
    "session": {"name": "s_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL", "start": SESSION_START, "lines": render(session_ns)},
    "workflow": {"name": "wf_FL_JAFFLESHOP_DEMO", "start": WF_START, "lines": render(wf_ns), "links": links},
    "targetColumns": target_cols,
    "lineage": lin,
    "flags": flags,
}

body = json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)

# ---- guard: no token of the command-task value may appear in the output ----
secret_lines = [n for n, t in LINES.items() if "VALUEPAIR" in t]
for n in secret_lines:
    value = html.unescape(dict(ATTR.findall(LINES[n])).get("VALUE", ""))
    tokens = {t for t in re.split(r"[\s\"@/:\\]+", value) if len(t) >= 5}
    leaked = [t for t in tokens if t in body]
    # Paths like "Informatica" or "server" are harmless words; the guard only cares about the login part.
    login = value.split("@")[0].split()[-1] if "@" in value else ""
    if login and login in body:
        raise SystemExit("GUARD FAILED: credential text found in output")
print("guard: no credential text in output")

with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write("/* GENERATED from the demo XML (%s) by a script. Do not edit by hand.\n" % data["xmlFile"])
    f.write("   Slice: RAW_ORDERS -> STG_ORDERS in mapping m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL, plus its session and workflow.\n")
    f.write("   Every line number is read from the file. Attributes are trimmed to the ones that matter. */\n")
    f.write("window.EXAMPLE = ")
    f.write(body)
    f.write(";\n")

print("nodes:", [(x["id"], x["start"], x["end"], x["instanceLine"]) for x in nodes])
print("wires:", data["wireCounts"])
print("session lines:", [r[0] for r in data["session"]["lines"]])
print("workflow lines:", [r[0] for r in data["workflow"]["lines"]])
print("flags:", flags)
print("lineage SUBTOTAL_CENTS:", [(s["n"], s["text"]) for s in lin["SUBTOTAL_CENTS"]])
print("lineage ORDERED_AT_DAY:", [(s["n"], s["text"]) for s in lin["ORDERED_AT_DAY"]])

for n in MAP_LINES:

    if p["tag"] == "CONNECTOR":

        if a["FROMINSTANCE"] in SLICE and a["TOINSTANCE"] in SLICE:

    if p["tag"] == "INSTANCE" and p["attrs"].get("NAME") in SLICE:
        instances[p["attrs"]["NAME"]] = n

nodes = []
for name in SLICE:
    ns = block(starts[name])
    keep_ns = []
    for n in ns:
        p = parse(n)
        if p["tag"] == "TABLEATTRIBUTE" and p["attrs"].get("NAME") not in SHOW_TABLEATTR:
            continue
        keep_ns.append(n)
    wires_in = sorted(n for n, a in connectors if a["TOINSTANCE"] == name)
    nodes.append({
        "id": name,
        "type": parse(starts[name])["attrs"].get("TYPE") or parse(starts[name])["tag"].title(),
        "start": ns[0], "end": ns[-1],
        "instanceLine": instances.get(name),
        "lines": render(keep_ns),
        "wiresIn": render(wires_in),
    })

SESSION_START = find("SESSION", "s_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL")
session_ns = [SESSION_START]
sess_block = block(SESSION_START)
for n in sess_block:
    p = parse(n)
    if not p or p["close"]:
        continue
    if p["tag"] == "SESSTRANSFORMATIONINST" and p["attrs"].get("SINSTANCENAME") in SLICE:
        session_ns.append(n)
writer = None
for n in sess_block:
    p = parse(n)
    if p and not p["close"] and p["tag"] == "SESSIONEXTENSION" and p["attrs"].get("SINSTANCENAME") == "STG_ORDERS" \

    p = parse(n)
    if p["tag"] in ("SESSIONEXTENSION", "CONNECTIONREFERENCE"):
        session_ns.append(n)

    if p and p["tag"] == "ATTRIBUTE" and p["attrs"].get("NAME") == "Treat source rows as":

def lineage(inst, port, out, depth=0):
    if depth > 20:
        raise SystemExit("lineage too deep")
    key = (inst, port)
    if inst == "RAW_ORDERS":
        out.append({"n": port_line[key], "text": "%s.%s" % (inst, port), "kind": "PC Source column"})
        return
    expr = port_expr.get(key)
    ptype = port_type.get(key, "")
    if expr is not None and ptype in ("OUTPUT", "LOCAL VARIABLE") and inst != "STG_ORDERS":
        out.append({"n": port_line[key], "text": "%s.%s = %s" % (inst, port, expr), "kind": "port expression"})
        names = set(IDENT.findall(QUOTED.sub("", expr)))
        for nm in sorted(names):

input.content:
PowerCenter → dbt explainer

PowerCenter → dbt converter

PowerCenter saves a data pipeline as an XML drawing of boxes and wires. dbt does the same job with plain SQL files. We are building a tool that reads the XML and writes the SQL.

The three parts

Input: the XML

A mapping is a chain of boxes (transformations). Connectors join one column to the next.

The session and workflow only say when things run, not what they compute.

See one mapping, piece by piece →

Converter: five steps

Turn the drawing into a graph, follow it back from each target, and turn every box into one SQL step (a CTE).

Hard parts: Informatica's own formula language, and boxes with no direct SQL twin.

Step through the five steps →

Output: dbt models

Each model is one select. A table written by one mapping and read by the next becomes a ref().

When the XML looks wrong, the SQL copies it and carries a flag.

See the SQL for one table →

What is in the XML, in numbers

Counted from the file with a script. Line references open the file on GitHub.

WhatCountDetail
Mappings3staging L90, enriched marts L1210, core marts L3107
Transformations (boxes)9824 + 45 + 29. Source Qualifier 28, Expression 25, Joiner 16, Sorter 15, Aggregator 9, Router 2, Union 2, Filter 1
Connectors (wires)1,066165 + 624 + 277
PC Sources / PC Targets12 / 16sources: 6 RAW_ + 6 STG_. targets: 6 STG_ + 5 core marts + 5 enriched marts
Port expressions384270 pass-through (201 same name, 69 renames) and 114 with real logic
Router conditions5e.g. REGION = 'APAC' L276
Logic to translate119114 + 5. Of the 114, 26 are helper variable ports

How we know the output is right

Decisions so far

D1 · Follow the connectors, not the names. When the XML looks wrong, copy what it does and add a flag. Don't fix it. First case: STG_ORDERS gets dollars in its *_CENTS columns L608–613. See it.

D2 · The reference is dbt-labs/jaffle-shop, not jaffle_shop_duckdb. The XML's 6 raw tables match it, and the demo README links it.

D3 · The workflow's command task holds a plaintext credential. We never show, copy or commit it. The demo XML stays out of git.

Open questions

O1 · How do we run jaffle-shop on DuckDB? Its main branch needs dbt 2.0 or newer, and its README doesn't list DuckDB. We tested three ways and all three built it (49 nodes passed). One has to be chosen.

O2 · One dbt model per PC Target? This is the plan, because one model builds exactly one table. The staging mapping alone would give 6 models.

O3 · Load behaviour. The session says Truncate target table = NO L919, so PowerCenter adds rows on every run. A dbt table is rebuilt instead. We note this difference and don't copy it.

O4 · Folder layout of the generated models, and which language the converter is written in.

Sources: the assignment brief, flowline-pwc-demo, and dbt-labs/jaffle-shop. Last updated 2026-11-21.

input.content:
PowerCenter → dbt explainer

Glossary

Our shared language. One word per idea, used the same way in code, tests, the README and our chats. This is what domain-driven design calls a ubiquitous language.

Words that clash. PowerCenter and dbt use some of the same words for different things. Say which side you mean every time:

Source: say PC Source or dbt source. Target: say PC Target; in dbt, a target is an environment like dev. Expression: say Expression transformation (the box) or port expression (the formula). Test: say data test (dbt) or unit test (ours). Link: only between workflow tasks; between ports it's a connector.

Terms

Tables at a glance

The pipeline runs in layers: raw → staging → marts. Each table in the XML, which mapping writes it, and its twin in the reference project. Note that raw stores become locations from staging onwards.

Table in the XMLDefined atWritten byjaffle-shop twin
Raw: the input data. PC Sources only, nothing writes them.
RAW_CUSTOMERSL40(seed data)raw_customers
RAW_ORDERSL26(seed data)raw_orders
RAW_ITEMSL35(seed data)raw_items
RAW_PRODUCTSL19(seed data)raw_products
RAW_STORESL13(seed data)raw_stores
RAW_SUPPLIESL6(seed data)raw_supplies
Staging: cleaned and renamed. Each is a PC Target here and a PC Source in the mart mappings.
STG_CUSTOMERSL86m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULLstg_customers
STG_ORDERSL67m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULLstg_orders
STG_ORDER_ITEMSL62m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULLstg_order_items
STG_PRODUCTSL52m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULLstg_products
STG_SUPPLIESL44m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULLstg_supplies
STG_LOCATIONSL79m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULLstg_locations (from raw_stores)
Core marts: the business tables.
CUSTOMERSL1199m_FL_JS_MARTS_COREcustomers
ORDERSL1185m_FL_JS_MARTS_COREorders
ORDER_ITEMSL1172m_FL_JS_MARTS_COREorder_items
PRODUCTSL1162m_FL_JS_MARTS_COREproducts
SUPPLIESL1154m_FL_JS_MARTS_COREsupplies
Enriched marts: extra tables. No twin, so check 3 can't cover them.
CUSTOMER_360L1133m_FL_JS_MARTS_ENRICHEDnone
ORDER_FINANCIALSL1112m_FL_JS_MARTS_ENRICHEDnone
ORDER_ITEM_ENRICHEDL1089m_FL_JS_MARTS_ENRICHEDnone
PRODUCT_DAILY_PERFORMANCEL1077m_FL_JS_MARTS_ENRICHEDnone
STORE_DAILY_KPISL1060m_FL_JS_MARTS_ENRICHEDnone

Both mart mappings read the STG_ tables. The enriched mapping does not read the core marts. jaffle-shop also has locations and metricflow_time_spine marts, which the XML doesn't have.

Terms live in assets/glossary-data.js. Add a term there and it shows up here and in every page's hover cards.

input.content:
PowerCenter → dbt explainer

One mapping, end to end

We follow one small path through the XML: raw orders in, STG_ORDERS out. It is short, but it touches every piece: a PC Source, three kinds of box, a PC Target, and the session and workflow that run it.

The path lives inside mapping m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL L90, which writes 6 PC Targets. Here we look at the orders path only. All XML on this page was pulled from the file by a script. Attributes are trimmed to the ones that matter, and line numbers open GitHub.

1 · Who runs it: workflow and session

The workflow runs tasks in order. Each session runs one mapping. Our path sits in the first session.

What the session adds

Runs mapping
m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL L811
Writes STG_ORDERS through
connection MART_Jaffleshop L912 (a name; the details live outside the file)
Load type
Bulk L913
Truncate target first?
NO L919, so every run adds rows
Treat source rows as
Insert L995

None of this changes what is computed. It is about how rows are written. dbt handles that with materialization, which is still an open question.


    

  


  
  
2 · The mapping path: click a box

  
Five instances joined by connectors. The number on each arrow is how many connectors run between the two boxes.

  

  


  
  
3 · Follow the connectors, not the names

  
The last hop, from the Sorter into the PC Target, is where names and connectors disagree. Toggle the view to see it.

  

    
    
  

  
  

    
What we do: the SQL copies the connectors exactly, so subtotal_cents really holds dollars, and every one of these columns gets a flag. This is decision D1: we copy the XML, we don't fix it.

  


  
  
4 · The output: what the converter should write

  
Hand-written for now, to show the target. Each box becomes one CTE, the Sorter disappears, and the final select copies the connectors, flags included.

  

    

      
      
    

    


-- Generated from mapping m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL, PC Target STG_ORDERS
-- Path: RAW_ORDERS → SQ_RAW_ORDERS → EXP_ORDERS → SRT_ORDERS → STG_ORDERS

with sq_raw_orders as (
    -- Source Qualifier SQ_RAW_ORDERS (XML L161–180): no override, no filter
    select id, customer, ordered_at, store_id, subtotal, tax_paid, order_total
    from {{ source('raw', 'raw_orders') }}
),

exp_orders as (
    -- Expression EXP_ORDERS (XML L106–125)
    select
        id                            as order_id,
        customer                      as customer_id,
        store_id                      as location_id,
        date_trunc('day', ordered_at) as ordered_at_day,
        subtotal / 100                as subtotal,
        tax_paid / 100                as tax_paid,
        order_total / 100             as order_total,
        subtotal                      as subtotal_cents,
        tax_paid                      as tax_paid_cents,
        order_total                   as order_total_cents
    from sq_raw_orders
)

-- Sorter SRT_ORDERS (XML L513–533) dropped: row order has no meaning in a table.

select
    order_id,
    customer_id,
    location_id,
    ordered_at_day,
    subtotal          as subtotal_cents,     -- FLAG: dollars into a *_CENTS column (XML L608)
    tax_paid          as tax_paid_cents,     -- FLAG: XML L609
    order_total       as order_total_cents,  -- FLAG: XML L610
    subtotal_cents    as subtotal,           -- FLAG: cents into a dollar column (XML L611)
    tax_paid_cents    as tax_paid,           -- FLAG: XML L612
    order_total_cents as order_total         -- FLAG: XML L613
from exp_orders

    

    


version: 2

sources:
  - name: raw                 # from PC Source OWNERNAME="RAW" (XML L26)
    schema: raw
    tables:
      - name: raw_orders      # from PC Source NAME="RAW_ORDERS" (XML L26)
        columns:
          - name: id
          - name: customer
          - name: ordered_at
          - name: store_id
          - name: subtotal
          - name: tax_paid
          - name: order_total

    

  

  
The folder name staging/ is a placeholder; folder layout is still open.


  
Does it run? One real row

  
We ran the SQL above in DuckDB on jaffle-shop's seed data, next to the reference model. Both return 61,948 rows. Here is the first order:

  

    

      
Columnraw_orders.csvOur stg_ordersReference stg_orders

      
        
order_id9bed808a-…9bed808a-…9bed808a-…

        
ordered_at_day2024-09-01T15:01:002024-09-01 00:002024-09-01 00:00 (named ordered_at)

        
subtotal_centssubtotal = 7007.0700

        
tax_paid_centstax_paid = 420.4242

        
order_total_centsorder_total = 7427.42742

        
subtotal7007.00

        
tax_paid420.42

        
order_total7427.42

      
    

  

  

    
Two lessons for check 3 (matching the reference):

    
1. A faithful converter will not match the reference on these 6 columns. That's expected, so the comparison has to know about flags.

    2. Column names differ too: ordered_at_day here (from the PC Target) and ordered_at in jaffle-shop. The comparison needs a column-name map.

  


  
Next: how the converter gets from the XML to this SQL, in five steps →

  
Data: assets/example-data.js, generated from the XML. Row check run on 2026-11-21 against jaffle-shop seeds in DuckDB.

One mapping, end to end

We follow one small path through the XML: raw orders in, STG_ORDERS out. It is short, but it touches every piece: a PC Source, three kinds of box, a PC Target, and the session and workflow that run it.

The path lives inside mapping m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL L90, which writes 6 PC Targets. Here we look at the orders path only. All XML on this page was pulled from the file by a script. Attributes are trimmed to the ones that matter, and line numbers open GitHub.

1 · Who runs it: workflow and session

The workflow runs tasks in order. Each session runs one mapping. Our path sits in the first session.

What the session adds

Runs mapping
m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL L811
Writes STG_ORDERS through
connection MART_Jaffleshop L912 (a name; the details live outside the file)
Load type
Bulk L913
Truncate target first?
NO L919, so every run adds rows
Treat source rows as
Insert L995

None of this changes what is computed. It is about how rows are written. dbt handles that with materialization, which is still an open question.


    

  


  
  
2 · The mapping path: click a box

  
Five instances joined by connectors. The number on each arrow is how many connectors run between the two boxes.

  

  


  
  
3 · Follow the connectors, not the names

  
The last hop, from the Sorter into the PC Target, is where names and connectors disagree. Toggle the view to see it.

  

    
    
  

  
  

    
What we do: the SQL copies the connectors exactly, so subtotal_cents really holds dollars, and every one of these columns gets a flag. This is decision D1: we copy the XML, we don't fix it.

  


  
  
4 · The output: what the converter should write

  
Hand-written for now, to show the target. Each box becomes one CTE, the Sorter disappears, and the final select copies the connectors, flags included.

  

    

      
      
    

    


-- Generated from mapping m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL, PC Target STG_ORDERS
-- Path: RAW_ORDERS → SQ_RAW_ORDERS → EXP_ORDERS → SRT_ORDERS → STG_ORDERS

with sq_raw_orders as (
    -- Source Qualifier SQ_RAW_ORDERS (XML L161–180): no override, no filter
    select id, customer, ordered_at, store_id, subtotal, tax_paid, order_total
    from {{ source('raw', 'raw_orders') }}
),

exp_orders as (
    -- Expression EXP_ORDERS (XML L106–125)
    select
        id                            as order_id,
        customer                      as customer_id,
        store_id                      as location_id,
        date_trunc('day', ordered_at) as ordered_at_day,
        subtotal / 100                as subtotal,
        tax_paid / 100                as tax_paid,
        order_total / 100             as order_total,
        subtotal                      as subtotal_cents,
        tax_paid                      as tax_paid_cents,
        order_total                   as order_total_cents
    from sq_raw_orders
)

-- Sorter SRT_ORDERS (XML L513–533) dropped: row order has no meaning in a table.

select
    order_id,
    customer_id,
    location_id,
    ordered_at_day,
    subtotal          as subtotal_cents,     -- FLAG: dollars into a *_CENTS column (XML L608)
    tax_paid          as tax_paid_cents,     -- FLAG: XML L609
    order_total       as order_total_cents,  -- FLAG: XML L610
    subtotal_cents    as subtotal,           -- FLAG: cents into a dollar column (XML L611)
    tax_paid_cents    as tax_paid,           -- FLAG: XML L612
    order_total_cents as order_total         -- FLAG: XML L613
from exp_orders

        columns:
          - name: id
          - name: customer
          - name: ordered_at
          - name: store_id
          - name: subtotal
          - name: tax_paid
          - name: order_total

The explainer is built and set up for git. Nothing is committed yet; the file list and message are at the bottom.

## Your correction
You were right. Checked with an XML parser:
- **384 port expressions.** 270 just pass a column through (201 keep the same name, 69 are renames) and 114 have real logic.
- **Plus 5 Router conditions**, so **119 logic expressions** in total to translate. 26 of the 114 are helper variables, not output columns.
- My "389" was a raw line count that mixed both kinds together.

## How to open it
```bash
open docs/index.html
```
It's also open in the app's browser pane now, at `http://localhost:8765`. I tested everything through that local server. Opening the file directly should work the same, since the pages load nothing over the network, but I couldn't test that path here.

**What's in it** (4 pages, sharing one menu):
- **Overview:** the input → converter → output diagram, the XML counts, the 3 checks, a decisions log (D1–D3) and open questions.
- **Glossary:** 51 terms in three groups (PowerCenter, dbt, our converter).
  - A box lists words that mean different things on each side, like *Source* and *Target*.
  - A table lists all 22 tables with their jaffle-shop equivalent.
  - Dotted words on every page show a hover card from this glossary.
- **One mapping, end to end:** RAW_ORDERS → STG_ORDERS.
  - The workflow and session that run it.
  - Clickable boxes that show the real XML lines.
  - A diagram of the cents/dollars swap.
  - The target dbt SQL and `sources.yml`.
- **The 5 steps:** parse, graph, walk, translate and write, applied to the same example. There's a column picker that traces any target column back to the raw table.

## What I checked
- **Line numbers:** a script checked all 76 cited lines against the XML. The example data is pulled from the file by a script, not typed by hand.
- **The example SQL:** I ran it on jaffle-shop's seed data in DuckDB and got 61,948 rows, the same as the reference. For the first order it gives `subtotal_cents = 7.0`, while the reference gives `700`.
- **Display:** dark and light mode, phone width with no sideways scrolling, and no console errors.

## Two findings worth knowing
- **The swap looks like ports joined by position.** In the file's own order every connector goes straight across. The target just lists its `*_CENTS` columns first.
- **The reference check needs two extras.**
  - *Flags:* a faithful converter won't match the reference on those 6 swapped columns.
  - *A column-name map:* column names differ too, e.g. `ordered_at_day` here vs `ordered_at` in jaffle-shop.

## The credential
- It isn't in any page or file to be committed. I scanned all 10 files, and the XML stays in the ignored `external/` folder.
- One problem: it did appear once in raw command output during my first reply, before your instruction. If you export this conversation for the submission, remove it from that file first.

## DuckDB: it runs, but you need to pick how
jaffle-shop's `main` needs dbt 2.0 or newer, and its README doesn't list DuckDB. I tried three ways and all built the project (49 of 49 passed; customers 935 rows, orders 61,948):

| Option | What | Catch |
|---|---|---|
| A | dbt v2 (2.0.12) on `main` | It has an older DuckDB built in, which couldn't open a database file written by the current DuckDB Python package (2.0.1) |
| B | dbt-core 1.12.7 + dbt-duckdb on `main` | Every command needs `--no-version-check` to get past the version rule |
| C | dbt-core 1.12.7 + dbt-duckdb on commit `7d0d8de` | Pinned to an older commit. Only the README, Taskfile and config changed after it; the models are identical to `main` |

**I recommend C.** It gives the same models as `main` with standard open-source dbt, no flags, and one DuckDB version for everything. Which do you want?

## Proposed commit
These 10 files go in. `external/` (both clones) is ignored.
```
.gitignore
.claude/launch.json        (optional: lets the app preview docs/)
docs/index.html  docs/glossary.html  docs/example.html  docs/process.html
docs/assets/site.css  site.js  glossary-data.js  example-data.js
```
```
Add project scaffold and interactive explainer pages

Set up the repo for the PowerCenter → dbt take-home and add a small
multi-page HTML explainer in docs/ that we will grow as we go:

- index.html: overview of input, converter and output, XML counts,
  decisions so far and open questions
- glossary.html: shared vocabulary (PowerCenter, dbt, converter terms)
  and a table of every table in the pipeline
- example.html: one path (RAW_ORDERS → STG_ORDERS) with its workflow,
  session, boxes, the cents/dollars connector swap, and the target SQL
- process.html: the five converter steps applied to that path
- assets/example-data.js: generated from the demo XML so every line
  number is real

.gitignore keeps third-party clones (external/) out of git, including
the demo XML, which contains a plaintext credential.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```
The script that generates `example-data.js` is in my scratchpad, not the repo. We can add it once we've picked the converter's language.
