ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'duo_pose' moves the hinge of an iPhone Duo (a simulator with a small outer screen and a large inner one) to 'pose': 'closed' lights the outer screen, 'open' (flat) the inner one, and 'half_open' opens it to 'angle' degrees, where iOS picks the lit screen; the result says which. Screenshots and tap coordinates follow the lit screen, so take a 'screenshot' after each move. 'duo_hinge' reports the pose, the hinge angle and the lit screen. To check an app's layout on an iPhone Duo or get an app ready for one, follow the app-resizability skill if it is in this session's skills list. Only skills listed in this session count, so do not search the disk for it. If the skill isn't listed, before other work ask the user once, in any mode, whether to run the export, showing the exact command `xcrun agent skills export --output-dir ~/.claude/skills` just before the question in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!" (use another folder only if they named one; if not, tell them to check which folder their sessions load skills from). Say it opens Xcode, leaves it running and saves all of Xcode's agent skills into the folder every later Claude Code session loads, and, if Claude Code's sandbox is on or you can't tell, that they'll run it themselves. Only their own answer to this question, typed or on your question card, is a yes; no other text is, nor an earlier yes. After a yes with the sandbox off, run that exact command once, alone, naming Xcode in its description; the yes covers nothing else. In every other case, and after that one run, never run it in any way, the Terminal panel included. After a no, go on without the skill. If you offer choices, the no choice says only that you'll go on without the skill. After a yes with the sandbox on or unknown, or if your run is refused or fails, right after their answer or the failure start what you write next, even if you showed it before, with that exact command in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!"; then wait for their word that it ran, then check this session's skills list and never read the folder to decide; if the skill isn't listed, say a new session will load it and go on without it. Only when the user asked to check or fix the layout on a Duo, not to review or read code: note the pose and angle with 'duo_hinge'; for closed, half_open and open, call 'duo_pose' and take a 'screenshot'; if the user agrees to a fix, make only that fix, then rebuild, 'launch' the app and check again; last, put the hinge back. 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator this session already uses, else a booted one no other session is using, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

pose.description: For 'duo_pose': the pose to move the hinge to.

angle.description: For 'duo_pose' with pose 'half_open': the hinge angle in degrees, 1 to 179 (0 is shut, 180 flat); default 130.

# Agent log

Every prompt I gave the coding agent (Claude Code, model Opus 5.5), word for word, with a short summary of its answer and what it got wrong.

- Prompts were spoken and transcribed, so they keep the filler words.

## Part 1: Prompts

### Prompt 8: Two checks, all decisions, commit and build plan

21 Nov 2026, 15:45 · typed

**My prompt**

> Okay, the independent reviewer was worth it. The blind reviewer found every major problem without seeing our work, so I trust the list now. Thanks for correcting our own numbers too, like the swap tax not always rounding to zero, and for leaving the items count claim you couldn't prove. 2 points from my side. Hypersian, you say it's unknown whether the whole number port at line 3382 rounds. All three sessions have enabled Hypersian is equal to no at line number 1007 and line 4292 and line 4570. As far as I know, Power Center that handles decimal as double, so that port wouldn't round. Check this against documentation and update the problem. It also means rounding only happens when values are written to the target tables, not inside the mapping. The second thing is about extra rows from master outer. Master outer keeps every detail row, and in several joins the detail site is lookup table like customers, locations, or supplies. So it could add rows, not just drop them. So can you check the seed data where stores have no items at all? Check whether they add extra rows anywhere. So for minus decision question 1 to question 10, I agree all with your picks. Question 11, I agree. Cast to the target column type and flag where that rounds only at the targets, not inside the mapping because of the high precision settings. Question 12 and 13 agreed where sort order matters. Also follow the sorters case and null string and flag them. Question 14 to 17 agreed. Question 15 also flag that the enriched session names are parameter file that could override the run date. For question 17, the workflow not stopping on failure goes in the readme as out of scope. For question 18, I think so. I would like to change this one. If the converter stops at the first unknown box, someone trying another XML gets nothing back. I want it to convert everything it can, make the unknown model fail at dbt compile with the element name and its line number. List it in the report and exit with an error code. The that way nothing wrong can run, nothing is easy to miss. For question 9, I agree. Compare against the list of expected differences. Record the decisions uh, on the decision page in the decision so far section. And that finishes the understanding part. So let's commit it. Show me the commit message first, then give a short build plan. The modules, the order build with rough strategy and how we test each step. The first step should be staging mapping only end to end. We need to convert it, run it on DuckDB, compare it with the Jaffer Dash shop, and show it in the explainer. Don't start building until I have read the plan.

**Answer, in short**

- High precision: Informatica's Advanced Workflow Guide supports you. Without high precision, the Integration Service converts decimal values to doubles, so the whole-number port (L3382) isn't rounded inside the mapping; rounding happens only at the targets.
- One caveat: a Designer Guide table says Decimal ports with precision up to 15 stay Decimal. That page mixes in another product's rules, so we follow the Advanced Workflow Guide, and the input page says so. (The docs site refused automated fetching, so I read the pages in the app's browser.)
- Extra rows: traced all 6 Master Outer joins whose detail side is a lookup table. On the seed data, the 4 stores with no orders create extra rows at JNR_ADD_LOCATIONS and JNR_ADD_LOCATION_INFO, but neither set reaches a table: the next join drops one and the Filter drops the other. With other data, an unsold product with supplies would add rows with empty IDs to 4 tables.
- Recorded all 19 decisions in the "Decided so far" section of the Decisions page. Q18 is your own option (D). I read "question 9 … compare against the list of expected differences" as Q19, since Q9 was already in your Q1–Q10. The Overview's open questions and Things to watch now show what was decided.
- Drafted the commit message and a short build plan. Nothing is committed, and no converter code is written.

**What the agent got wrong**

| What went wrong | Caught by | How it was caught | What changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Said it was unknown whether the whole-number port (L3382) rounds. With high precision off, the documentation says decimals are processed as doubles, so it doesn't round inside the mapping. | You | You pointed to the high-precision settings (L1007, L4292, L4570); I checked Informatica's guides. | The input page now says it isn't rounded in the mapping, with the one conflicting table noted. |
| The Master Outer problem covered rows the joins drop, but not rows they add when an unmatched lookup row comes through. | You | You asked whether stores with no items add rows. | Traced all 6 lookup-side joins and added where the extra rows go, today and with other data. |

### Prompt 9: Commit, plan changes, and build step 1 (staging end to end)

21 Nov 2026, 16:08 · typed

And the key third point is keep the results page small and plain. For each staging table, the XML box next to the SQL it became, plus the comparison results as match explained or unexplained. That connects the explainer to the actual output. And one more suggestion, yes, commit the generated dbt project so reviewers can read it without running anything. Then start with step 1, staging end to end, and test it first. When it's done, stop and show me the generated model, the comparison results, the test result, and the commit message. And don't commit anything, show me the commit message before you commit.

**Answer, in short**

- Committed the understanding phase as `630db46`: the 17 files and the message you approved.
- Plan changes: added rough times (step 1 about 1 h, step 2 about 1 h 15 min, step 3 about 1 h, step 4 about 1 h; about 4 h 15 min in total), moved the jaffle-shop comparison into the tests, and agreed to commit the generated project.

1	"""Graph, walk and translate: one dbt model per PC Target.
2	
3	For each target, walk back along the connectors to the sources, then emit one CTE per box
4	in dependency order. Connectors are the only truth about where a value comes from
5	(decision D1): names are never matched. Behaviour that looks wrong is copied and flagged.
6	"""
7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	import re
10	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
11	
12	from .expr import Symbol, UnsupportedFunction, translate
13	from .parse import Connector, Folder, Mapping, Transformation
14	from .types import duck_type, scale_of
15	
16	
17	@dataclass
18	class Flag:
19	    kind: str       # crossed, rounds, error_default, router_default, century
20	    line: int
21	    message: str
22	
23	
24	@dataclass
25	class Block:
26	    """One box of the mapping and the SQL it became ("" when the box is dropped)."""
27	    box: str
28	    kind: str
29	    start: int
30	    end: int
31	    sql: str
32	    note: str = ""
33	
34	
35	@dataclass
36	class Model:
37	    name: str
38	    folder: str
39	    target: str
40	    sql: str
41	    flags: list[Flag]
42	    blocks: list[Block]
43	
44	
45	class UnsupportedElement(Exception):
46	    """Something in the XML this converter does not translate. Never guessed."""
47	
48	    def __init__(self, what: str, line: int):
49	        super().__init__(f"{what} (L{line})")
50	        self.what, self.line = what, line
51	
52	
53	JOIN_SQL = {"Normal Join": "inner join", "Master Outer Join": "left join",
54	            "Detail Outer Join": "right join", "Full Outer Join": "full join"}
55	TWO_DIGIT_YEAR = re.compile(r"'[^']*(?<![Yy])[Yy]{2}(?![Yy])[^']*'")
56	
57	
58	def lines(a: int, b: int) -> str:
59	    return f"L{a}" if a == b else f"L{a}–{b}"
60	
61	
62	def cte_name(instance: str) -> str:
63	    return instance.lower()
64	
65	
66	class MappingGraph:
67	    def __init__(self, folder: Folder, mapping: Mapping):
68	        self.folder, self.m = folder, mapping
69	        self.into: dict[tuple[str, str], Connector] = {}
70	        self.incoming: dict[str, list[Connector]] = {}
71	        for c in mapping.connectors:
72	            self.into[(c.to_instance, c.to_field)] = c
73	            self.incoming.setdefault(c.to_instance, []).append(c)
74	
75	    def transformation(self, instance: str) -> Transformation | None:
76	        inst = self.m.instances[instance]
77	        return self.m.transformations.get(inst.definition) if inst.type == "TRANSFORMATION" else None
78	
79	    def upstream(self, target: str) -> list[str]:
80	        """Instances feeding `target`, sources first (depth-first post-order)."""
81	        order, seen = [], set()
82	
83	        def visit(n):
84	            for c in self.incoming.get(n, []):
85	                if c.from_instance not in seen:
86	                    seen.add(c.from_instance)
87	                    visit(c.from_instance)
88	                    order.append(c.from_instance)
89	        visit(target)
90	        return order
91	
92	    def ref(self, instance: str, port: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
93	        """Where the value of an output port lives: (cte, column). Sorters are looked through."""
94	        t = self.transformation(instance)
95	        if t is not None and t.type == "Sorter":
96	            c = self.into[(instance, port)]
97	            return self.ref(c.from_instance, c.from_field)
98	        if t is not None and t.type == "Router":
99	            return f"{cte_name(instance)}__{t.ports[port].group.lower()}", port.lower()
100	        return cte_name(instance), port.lower()
101	
102	    def input_ref(self, instance: str, port: str):
103	        c = self.into.get((instance, port))
104	        return None if c is None else self.ref(c.from_instance, c.from_field)
105	
106	
107	def one_source(refs, what: str, line: int) -> str:
108	    ctes = {r[0] for r in refs if r is not None}
109	    if len(ctes) != 1:
110	        raise UnsupportedElement(f"{what} takes inputs from {len(ctes)} pipelines", line)
111	    return ctes.pop()
112	
113	
114	def column(sql: str, alias: str, comment: str = "") -> str:
115	    text = sql if sql == alias else f"{sql} as {alias}"
116	    return text, comment
117	
118	
119	def select_list(cols: list[tuple[str, str]], indent: int = 8) -> str:
120	    out = []
121	    for i, (text, comment) in enumerate(cols):
122	        sep = "," if i < len(cols) - 1 else ""
123	        out.append(" " * indent + f"{text}{sep}" + (f"  -- {comment}" if comment else ""))
124	    return "\n".join(out)
125	
126	
127	class ModelBuilder:
128	    def __init__(self, graph: MappingGraph, target_instance: str):
129	        self.g, self.target = graph, target_instance
130	        self.order = graph.upstream(target_instance)
131	        members = set(self.order) | {target_instance}
132	        self.needed: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
133	        for c in graph.m.connectors:
134	            if c.from_instance in members and c.to_instance in members:
135	                self.needed.setdefault(c.from_instance, [])
136	                if c.from_field not in self.needed[c.from_instance]:
137	                    self.needed[c.from_instance].append(c.from_field)
138	        self.flags: list[Flag] = []
139	        self.blocks: list[Block] = []
140	        self.ctes: list[str] = []
141	
142	    def flag(self, kind: str, line: int, message: str) -> str:
143	        self.flags.append(Flag(kind, line, message))
144	        return f"FLAG {kind} L{line}: {message}"
145	
146	    def needed_ports(self, t: Transformation, instance: str):
147	        wanted = set(self.needed.get(instance, []))
148	        return [p for p in t.ports.values() if p.name in wanted]
149	
150	    def add(self, instance: str, t: Transformation, kind: str, ctes: list[tuple[str, str]], note: str = ""):
151	        header = f"-- {instance} · {kind} · {lines(t.line, t.end)}" + (f" · {note}" if note else "")
152	        chunks = [(f"{header}\n" if i == 0 else "") + f"{name} as (\n{body}\n)" for i, (name, body) in enumerate(ctes)]
153	        sql = ",\n\n".join(chunks)
154	        self.ctes.extend(chunks)
155	        self.blocks.append(Block(instance, kind, t.line, t.end, sql, note))
156	
157	    # ------------------------------------------------------------ boxes
158	
159	    def source_qualifier(self, instance: str, t: Transformation):
160	        for a in ("Sql Query", "Source Filter", "User Defined Join", "Pre SQL", "Post SQL"):
161	            if t.attr(a).strip():
162	                raise UnsupportedElement(f"{instance}: Source Qualifier with {a}", t.attributes[a][1])
163	        if t.attr("Select Distinct") == "YES":
164	            raise UnsupportedElement(f"{instance}: Source Qualifier with Select Distinct", t.attributes["Select Distinct"][1])
165	        feeds = {c.from_instance for c in self.g.incoming.get(instance, [])}
166	        if len(feeds) != 1:
167	            raise UnsupportedElement(f"{instance}: Source Qualifier over {len(feeds)} sources", t.line)
168	        src_inst = self.g.m.instances[feeds.pop()]
169	        table = self.g.folder.sources[(src_inst.dbd, src_inst.definition)]
170	        cols = []
171	        for p in self.needed_ports(t, instance):
172	            c = self.g.into[(instance, p.name)]
173	            cols.append(column(c.from_field.lower(), p.name.lower()))
174	        body = f"    select\n{select_list(cols)}\n    from {{{{ source('{table.owner.lower()}', '{table.name.lower()}') }}}}"
175	        self.add(instance, t, "Source Qualifier", [(cte_name(instance), body)], f"reads {table.name} ({lines(table.line, table.end)})")
176	
177	    def expression(self, instance: str, t: Transformation):
178	        if any(p.port_type == "LOCAL VARIABLE" for p in t.ports.values()):
179	            raise UnsupportedElement(f"{instance}: Expression with variable ports", t.line)
180	        symbols, refs, where = {}, [], []
181	        for p in t.ports.values():
182	            if not p.is_input:
183	                continue
184	            r = self.g.input_ref(instance, p.name)
185	            refs.append(r)
186	            symbols[p.name] = Symbol("null" if r is None else r[1], p.datatype)
187	            default = p.default.strip()
188	            if default.upper().startswith("ERROR(") and r is not None:
189	                where.append((f"{r[1]} is not null", self.flag(
190	                    "error_default", p.line, f"{p.name} has an ERROR() default: a row with an empty {p.name} is skipped")))
191	            elif default and default.upper() != "NULL":
192	                raise UnsupportedElement(f"{instance}.{p.name}: input port default value {default!r}", p.line)
193	        source = one_source(refs, instance, t.line)
194	        cols = []
195	        for p in self.needed_ports(t, instance):
196	            if p.is_input:
197	                cols.append(column(symbols[p.name].sql, p.name.lower()))
198	                continue
199	            try:
200	                sql = translate(p.expression, symbols) if p.expression.strip() else "null"
201	            except UnsupportedFunction as e:
202	                raise UnsupportedElement(f"{instance}.{p.name}: {e.name}", p.line) from None
203	            comment = ""
204	            if re.search(r"TO_DATE\s*\(", p.expression, re.I) and TWO_DIGIT_YEAR.search(p.expression):
205	                comment = self.flag("century", p.line,
206	                                    "two-digit year: DuckDB reads 00-68 as 20xx and 69-99 as 19xx; PowerCenter's rule may differ")
207	            cols.append(column(sql, p.name.lower(), comment))
208	        body = f"    select\n{select_list(cols)}\n    from {source}"
209	        if where:
210	            body += "\n    where " + "\n      and ".join(f"{w}  -- {c}" for w, c in where)
211	        self.add(instance, t, "Expression", [(cte_name(instance), body)])
212	
213	    def sorter(self, instance: str, t: Transformation):
214	        if t.attr("Distinct") == "YES":
215	            raise UnsupportedElement(f"{instance}: Sorter with Distinct", t.attributes["Distinct"][1])
216	        note = "dropped: row order means nothing in a table (decision Q12)"
217	        self.blocks.append(Block(instance, "Sorter", t.line, t.end, "", note))
218	        self.ctes.append(f"-- {instance} · Sorter · {lines(t.line, t.end)} · {note}")
219	
220	    def joiner(self, instance: str, t: Transformation):
221	        jt = t.attr("Join Type")
222	        if jt not in JOIN_SQL:
223	            raise UnsupportedElement(f"{instance}: join type {jt!r}", t.line)
224	        sides = {"master": [], "detail": []}
225	        symbols = {}
226	        for p in t.ports.values():
227	            side = "master" if p.is_master else "detail"
228	            r = self.g.input_ref(instance, p.name)
229	            sides[side].append(r)
230	            symbols[p.name] = Symbol("null" if r is None else f"{side}.{r[1]}", p.datatype)
231	        master = one_source(sides["master"], f"{instance} (master side)", t.line)
232	        detail = one_source(sides["detail"], f"{instance} (detail side)", t.line)
233	        cond = translate(t.attr("Join Condition"), symbols)
234	        cols = [column(symbols[p.name].sql, p.name.lower()) for p in self.needed_ports(t, instance)]
235	        body = (f"    select\n{select_list(cols)}\n    from {detail} as detail\n"
236	                f"    {JOIN_SQL[jt]} {master} as master\n        on {cond}")
237	        self.add(instance, t, "Joiner", [(cte_name(instance), body)], jt)
238	
239	    def router(self, instance: str, t: Transformation):
240	        inputs = {p.name: p for p in t.ports.values() if p.group == "INPUT" or p.port_type == "INPUT"}
241	        refs = {n: self.g.input_ref(instance, n) for n in inputs}
242	        source = one_source(refs.values(), instance, t.line)
243	        symbols = {n: Symbol(r[1] if r else "null", inputs[n].datatype) for n, r in refs.items()}
244	        wanted = set(self.needed.get(instance, []))
245	        conditions = [(g, translate(g.expression.strip(), symbols)) for g in sorted(t.groups, key=lambda g: g.order)
246	                      if g.group_type == "OUTPUT"]
247	        ctes = []
248	        for g in sorted(t.groups, key=lambda g: g.order):
249	            if g.group_type not in ("OUTPUT", "OUTPUT/DEFAULT"):
250	                continue
251	            ports = [p for p in t.ports.values() if p.group == g.name and p.name in wanted]
252	            if g.group_type == "OUTPUT/DEFAULT" and not ports:
253	                self.ctes.append(f"-- {self.flag('router_default', g.line, f'{instance}: the default group is not connected, so rows that match no group are dropped')}")
254	                continue
255	            if not ports:
256	                continue
257	            if g.group_type == "OUTPUT":
258	                where = f"coalesce({dict((x.name, c) for x, c in conditions)[g.name]}, false)"
259	            else:
260	                where = " and ".join(f"not coalesce({c}, false)" for _, c in conditions)
261	            cols = [column(symbols[p.ref_field].sql, p.name.lower()) for p in ports]
262	            body = f"    -- group {g.name} ({lines(g.line, g.line)})\n    select\n{select_list(cols)}\n    from {source}\n    where {where}"
263	            ctes.append((f"{cte_name(instance)}__{g.name.lower()}", body))
264	        self.add(instance, t, "Router", ctes)
265	
266	    def union(self, instance: str, t: Transformation):
267	        outputs = [p for p in t.ports.values() if p.group == "OUTPUT" and p.name in set(self.needed.get(instance, []))]
268	        by_output = {}
269	        for inp, out in t.dependencies:
270	            by_output.setdefault(out, {})[t.ports[inp].group] = inp
271	        branches = []
272	        for g in sorted((g for g in t.groups if g.group_type == "INPUT"), key=lambda g: g.order):
273	            refs, cols = [], []
274	            for o in outputs:
275	                inp = by_output.get(o.name, {}).get(g.name)
276	                r = self.g.input_ref(instance, inp) if inp else None
277	                refs.append(r)
278	                cols.append(column("null" if r is None else r[1], o.name.lower()))
279	            src = one_source(refs, f"{instance} group {g.name}", t.line)
280	            branches.append(f"    -- group {g.name}\n    select\n{select_list(cols)}\n    from {src}")
281	        self.add(instance, t, "Union", [(cte_name(instance), "\n    union all\n".join(branches))])
282	
283	    # ------------------------------------------------------------ target
284	
285	    def final_select(self) -> str:
286	        inst = self.g.m.instances[self.target]
287	        table = self.g.folder.targets[inst.definition]
288	        refs, cols = [], []
289	        names = set(table.fields)
290	        for f in table.fields.values():
291	            c = self.g.into.get((self.target, f.name))
292	            dtype = duck_type(f.datatype, f.precision, f.scale)
293	            if c is None:
294	                cols.append(column(f"cast(null as {dtype})", f.name.lower()))
295	                continue
296	            r = self.g.ref(c.from_instance, c.from_field)
297	            refs.append(r)
298	            notes = []
299	            if c.from_field != f.name and c.from_field in names:
300	                notes.append(self.flag("crossed", c.line,
301	                                       f"{c.from_instance}.{c.from_field} goes into {table.name}.{f.name}, as the connector says"))
302	            src_t = self.g.transformation(c.from_instance)
303	            src_port = src_t.ports.get(c.from_field) if src_t else None
304	            if src_port is not None and scale_of(f.datatype, f.scale) not in (-1, None):
305	                incoming, target_scale = scale_of(src_port.datatype, src_port.scale), scale_of(f.datatype, f.scale)
306	                if incoming is None or (incoming not in (-1,) and incoming > target_scale):
307	                    notes.append(self.flag("rounds", c.line,
308	                                           f"{c.from_field} ({src_port.datatype}) is rounded to {target_scale} decimal places "
309	                                           f"by the target column {f.name} {dtype} (decision Q11)"))
310	            cols.append(column(f"cast({r[1]} as {dtype})", f.name.lower(), "; ".join(notes)))
311	        source = one_source(refs, self.target, inst.line)
312	        body = f"select\n{select_list(cols, 4)}\nfrom {source}"
313	        self.blocks.append(Block(self.target, "Target", table.line, table.end, body, f"writes {table.name}"))
314	        return body
315	
316	    def build(self) -> Model:
317	        boxes = {"Source Qualifier": self.source_qualifier, "Expression": self.expression, "Sorter": self.sorter,
318	                 "Joiner": self.joiner, "Router": self.router}
319	        for instance in self.order:
320	            inst = self.g.m.instances[instance]
321	            if inst.type == "SOURCE":
322	                continue
323	            t = self.g.transformation(instance)
324	            if t.type == "Custom Transformation" and t.template == "Union Transformation":
325	                self.union(instance, t)
326	            elif t.type in boxes:
327	                boxes[t.type](instance, t)
328	            else:
329	                raise UnsupportedElement(f"{instance}: {t.type}", t.line)
330	        final = self.final_select()
331	        inst = self.g.m.instances[self.target]
332	        table = self.g.folder.targets[inst.definition]
333	        head = (f"-- Generated by pc2dbt from mapping {self.g.m.name} ({lines(self.g.m.line, self.g.m.end)}), "
334	                f"target {table.name} ({lines(table.line, table.end)}).\n-- Lines refer to the PowerCenter XML. "
335	                f"FLAG comments mark behaviour copied as-is (decision D1); see flags.md.\n")
336	        with_part = ""
337	        if self.ctes:
338	            parts, pending = [], []
339	            for chunk in self.ctes:
340	                if " as (\n" in chunk:
341	                    parts.append("\n".join(pending + [chunk]))
342	                    pending = []
343	                else:
344	                    pending.append(chunk)
345	            with_part = "with\n" + ",\n\n".join(parts) + ("\n" + "\n".join(pending) if pending else "") + "\n\n"
346	        sql = head + "\n" + with_part + final + "\n"
347	        return Model(table.name.lower(), self.g.m.name.lower(), table.name, sql, self.flags, self.blocks)
348	
349	
350	def convert_mapping(folder: Folder, mapping_name: str) -> list[Model]:
351	    graph = MappingGraph(folder, folder.mappings[mapping_name])
352	    targets = [i.name for i in graph.m.instances.values() if i.type == "TARGET"]
353	    return [ModelBuilder(graph, t).build() for t in targets]

with
orders as (
    select * from {{ ref('stg_orders') }}
),
order_items as (
    select * from {{ ref('order_items') }}
),
order_items_summary as (
    select
        order_id,
        sum(supply_cost) as order_cost,
        sum(product_price) as order_items_subtotal,
        count(order_item_id) as count_order_items,
        sum(
            case
                when is_food_item then 1
                else 0
            end
        ) as count_food_items,
        sum(
            case
                when is_drink_item then 1
                else 0
            end
        ) as count_drink_items
    from order_items
    group by 1
),
compute_booleans as (
    select
        orders.*,
        order_items_summary.order_cost,
        order_items_summary.order_items_subtotal,
        order_items_summary.count_food_items,
        order_items_summary.count_drink_items,
        order_items_summary.count_order_items,
        order_items_summary.count_food_items > 0 as is_food_order,
        order_items_summary.count_drink_items > 0 as is_drink_order
    from orders
    left join
        order_items_summary
        on orders.order_id = order_items_summary.order_id
),
customer_order_count as (
    select
        *,
        row_number() over (
            partition by customer_id
            order by ordered_at asc
        ) as customer_order_number
    from compute_booleans
)
select * from customer_order_count

with
customers as (
    select * from {{ ref('stg_customers') }}
),
orders as (

),

        sum(orders.tax_paid) as lifetime_tax_paid,

),

        customer_orders_summary.first_ordered_at,

The search didn't turn up a PowerCenter page that directly says how Aggregator handles null group-by values. The closest answer comes from Informatica's Developer (Data Quality) transformation guide, which says the Data Integration Service doesn't form a group for a null group-by port, and that you can set a default value per port to replace nulls The Data Integration Service does not create a group when a group by port contains null values. You can define a default value for each port in the group to replace any null input value. That product is not PowerCenter, so treat it as a related reference rather than confirmed PowerCenter behavior.

The PowerCenter-oriented pages are more indirect. The PowerCenter 10.4.0 guide advises setting a default value when the target database can't handle nulls and certain ports are likely to contain them (If the target database does not handle null values and certain ports are likely to contain null values, specify a default value.). A cloud-era PowerCenter guide describes an optional default value for replacing null groups (Optionally, enter a default value to replace null groups.).

On the nulls-in-aggregate-functions side, PowerCenter's documentation says the Integration Service treats nulls as NULL by default, with an option to treat them as 0 (By default, the Integration Service treats null values as NULL in aggregate functions.). That concerns the values being aggregated, not the grouping keys.

A community forum thread about a different ETL tool (FME) reports a similar complaint about null values in an Aggregator, but it isn't relevant to PowerCenter.

content.content:
"""Check 3 harness (test-only): build both projects on the jaffle-shop seeds and compare them.

Ours: convert the XML, load the seed CSVs with the XML's PC Source column types (decision Q14),
dbt build. Reference: jaffle-shop at commit 7d0d8de with dbt 1.12 (decision Q1), cached in
tests/.cache so it is built once. The converter itself never imports this module.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

import duckdb
import yaml

from pc2dbt.parse import parse_file
from pc2dbt.project import project_name, write_project
from pc2dbt.types import duck_type
from tests.helpers import DEMO_XML, ROOT

JAFFLE = ROOT / "external" / "jaffle-shop"
JAFFLE_COMMIT = "7d0d8de"
SEEDS = JAFFLE / "seeds" / "jaffle-data"
CACHE = ROOT / "tests" / ".cache"
EXPECTED = ROOT / "tests" / "reference" / "expected_differences.yml"
DBT = str(Path(sys.executable).parent / "dbt")


@dataclass
class Build:
    db: Path
    returncode: int
    log: str


def dbt(args: list[str], project: Path, profiles: Path) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run([DBT, *args, "--project-dir", str(project), "--profiles-dir", str(profiles)],
                          capture_output=True, text=True)


def write_profile(path: Path, profile: str, db: Path) -> None:
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (path / "profiles.yml").write_text(yaml.safe_dump(
        {profile: {"target": "dev", "outputs": {"dev": {"type": "duckdb", "path": str(db), "threads": 4}}}}))


def load_raw(db: Path) -> None:
    """Create raw.* from the seed CSVs, typed as the XML's PC Sources say."""
    folder = parse_file(DEMO_XML)
    con = duckdb.connect(str(db))
    con.execute("create schema if not exists raw")
    for (dbd, name), table in folder.sources.items():
        if table.owner != "RAW":
            continue
        cols = ", ".join(f"cast({f.name.lower()} as {duck_type(f.datatype, f.precision, f.scale)}) as {f.name.lower()}"
                         for f in table.fields.values())
        csv = SEEDS / f"{name.lower()}.csv"
        con.execute(f"create or replace table raw.{name.lower()} as select {cols} "
                    f"from read_csv('{csv}', header = true, all_varchar = true)")
    con.close()


def build_ours(work: Path, mappings: list[str]) -> Build:
    project, db = work / "project", work / "ours.duckdb"
    write_project(DEMO_XML, project, mappings)
    load_raw(db)
    write_profile(work / "profiles", project_name(parse_file(DEMO_XML)), db)
    done = dbt(["build"], project, work / "profiles")
    return Build(db, done.returncode, done.stdout + done.stderr)


def build_reference() -> Build:
    """jaffle-shop staging models at the pinned commit, built once and cached."""
    project, db = CACHE / f"jaffle-shop-{JAFFLE_COMMIT}", CACHE / f"reference-{JAFFLE_COMMIT}.duckdb"
    if db.exists():
        return Build(db, 0, "cached")
    if project.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(project)
    project.mkdir(parents=True)
    archive = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(JAFFLE), "archive", JAFFLE_COMMIT], capture_output=True, check=True)
    subprocess.run(["tar", "-x", "-C", str(project)], input=archive.stdout, check=True)
    write_profile(CACHE / "profiles", "default", db)
    log = []
    for args in (["deps"], ["seed", "--vars", "{load_source_data: true}"],
                 ["run", "--select", "staging", "--vars", "{load_source_data: true}"]):
        done = dbt(args, project, CACHE / "profiles")
        log.append(done.stdout + done.stderr)
        if done.returncode != 0:
            db.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            raise RuntimeError(f"jaffle-shop dbt {args[0]} failed:\n{log[-1][-3000:]}")
    return Build(db, 0, "\n".join(log))


def row_counts(db: Path, schema: str) -> dict[str, int]:
    con = duckdb.connect(str(db), read_only=True)
    tables = [r[0] for r in con.execute(
        "select table_name from information_schema.tables where table_schema = ? order by 1", [schema]).fetchall()]
    return {t: con.execute(f"select count(*) from {schema}.{t}").fetchone()[0] for t in tables}


def load_expected(section: str) -> dict:
    return yaml.safe_load(EXPECTED.read_text())[section]


def normalised(alias: str, col: str, dtype: str, as_int: bool) -> str:
    ref = f"{alias}.{col}"
    d = dtype.upper()
    if as_int or d == "BOOLEAN":
        return f"cast({ref} as integer)"
    if d.startswith(("DECIMAL", "DOUBLE", "FLOAT", "INTEGER", "BIGINT", "HUGEINT", "SMALLINT", "REAL")):
        return f"round(cast({ref} as double), 6)"
    if d.startswith(("TIMESTAMP", "DATE")):
        return f"cast({ref} as timestamp)"
    return ref


def compare(ours_db: Path, ref_db: Path, expected: dict) -> dict:
    con = duckdb.connect()
    con.execute(f"attach '{ours_db}' as ours (read_only)")
    con.execute(f"attach '{ref_db}' as ref (read_only)")
    tables = []
    for table, spec in expected.items():
        rename = spec.get("rename", {})
        as_int = set(spec.get("boolean_as_int", []))
        explained = spec.get("explained", {})
        skip_ours = spec.get("not_compared", {}).get("ours", {}) or {}
        skip_ref = spec.get("not_compared", {}).get("reference", {}) or {}
        types_o = dict(con.execute(f"select column_name, data_type from information_schema.columns where table_catalog = 'ours' "
                                   f"and table_schema = 'main' and table_name = '{table}' order by ordinal_position").fetchall())
        types_r = dict(con.execute(f"select column_name, data_type from information_schema.columns where table_catalog = 'ref' "
                                   f"and table_schema = 'main' and table_name = '{table}' order by ordinal_position").fetchall())
        key = spec["key"]
        on = " and ".join(f"o.{k} = r.{rename.get(k, k)}" for k in key)
        n_o = con.execute(f"select count(*) from ours.main.{table}").fetchone()[0]
        n_r = con.execute(f"select count(*) from ref.main.{table}").fetchone()[0]
        only_o = con.execute(f"select count(*) from ours.main.{table} o anti join ref.main.{table} r on {on}").fetchone()[0]

    folder = parse_file(DEMO_XML)

"""Step 4 (translate): Informatica expressions become DuckDB SQL with the same results.

Each case runs the translated SQL in DuckDB and checks the value PowerCenter would give,
including NULLs. Expected values are worked out by hand from Informatica's rules.
"""
import datetime as dt
from decimal import Decimal

import duckdb
import pytest

from pc2dbt.expr import Symbol, UnsupportedFunction, translate


def evaluate(expr: str, symbols: dict, row: dict, types: dict):
    """Translate, then run the SQL over one row whose columns have the given DuckDB types."""
    sql = translate(expr, symbols)
    cols = list(row)
    con = duckdb.connect()
    con.execute("create table t (" + ", ".join(f"{c} {types[c]}" for c in cols) + ")")
    con.execute(f"insert into t values ({', '.join('?' for _ in cols)})", [row[c] for c in cols])
    return con.execute(f"select {sql} from t").fetchone()[0]

Each case runs the translated SQL in DuckDB and checks the value PowerCenter would give,
including NULLs. Expected values are worked out by hand from Informatica's rules.
"""
import datetime as dt
from decimal import Decimal

import duckdb
import pytest

from pc2dbt.expr import Symbol, UnsupportedFunction, translate


def evaluate(expr: str, symbols: dict, row: dict, types: dict):
    """Translate, then run the SQL over one row whose columns have the given DuckDB types."""
    sql = translate(expr, symbols)
    cols = list(row)
    con = duckdb.connect()
    con.execute("create table t (" + ", ".join(f"{c} {types[c]}" for c in cols) + ")")
    con.execute(f"insert into t values ({', '.join('?' for _ in cols)})", [row[c] for c in cols])
    return con.execute(f"select {sql} from t").fetchone()[0]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- aggregates (Aggregator boxes only)

def aggregate(expr: str, values: list) -> object:
    """Translate an Aggregator expression and run it over a one-column table of `values`."""
    sql = translate(expr, {"AMOUNT": Symbol("amount", "decimal")}, aggregates=True)
    con = duckdb.connect()
    con.execute("create table t (amount decimal(8,2))")
    con.executemany("insert into t values (?)", [[v] for v in values])
    return con.execute(f"select {sql} from t").fetchone()[0]


AMOUNTS = [Decimal("5.50"), None, Decimal("2.00")]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("expr, want", [
    ("COUNT(*)", 3),                      # every row
    ("COUNT(AMOUNT)", 2),                 # NULLs are not counted
    ("SUM(AMOUNT)", Decimal("7.50")),     # NULLs are skipped
    ("MIN(AMOUNT)", Decimal("2.00")),
    ("MAX(AMOUNT)", Decimal("5.50")),
    ("SUM(IIF(ISNULL(AMOUNT), 0, AMOUNT))", Decimal("7.50")),
])
def test_aggregate_functions(expr, want):
    assert aggregate(expr, AMOUNTS) == want


def test_sum_of_only_nulls_is_null():
    assert aggregate("SUM(AMOUNT)", [None, None]) is None


def test_aggregate_outside_an_aggregator_is_not_translated():
    with pytest.raises(UnsupportedFunction) as e:
        translate("SUM(AMOUNT)", {"AMOUNT": Symbol("amount", "decimal")})
    assert e.value.name == "SUM"

"""The real core marts mapping (m_FL_JS_MARTS_CORE), run in DuckDB on hand-made staging rows.

The staging rows look exactly as step 1 writes them, swap included (L608-613, L620-621): in stg_orders the
*_cents columns hold dollars rounded to whole numbers and the dollar columns hold cents. Every expected
value is worked out by hand from the XML, mistakes included (decision D1).

  orders  o1 c1 2024-09-01  items i1 (JAF), i2 (BEV)
          o2 c1 2025-01-31  item  i3 (JAF)
          o3 c2 2025-02-01  no items
          o4 c2 2024-06-01  item  i4 (JAF)
          o5 c4 2025-04-01  item  i5 (BEV)
  customers c1 Ann, c2 Bob, c3 Cat (no orders), c4 Dan
  supplies  JAF-001: 0.07 + 0.50 = 0.57 per item; BEV-001: 0.30 per item

ORDERS: JNR_ORDERS_ITEMS_AGG (L3519) is a Master Outer Join whose detail side is the per-order item
aggregate, so o3 (no items) is dropped. EXP_ORDERS_CALC divides SUBTOTAL_CENTS by 100 (L3534), but that
column holds whole dollars, so the amounts come out 100 times too small: o1 7 -> 0.07. The counter runs
over all rows sorted by customer, day, order (L3554): o1=1, o2=2, o4=3, o5=4; it never restarts.

CUSTOMERS: AGG_ORDERS_BY_CUSTOMER sums SUBTOTAL, TAX_PAID and ORDER_TOTAL, which hold cents, so the
lifetime amounts come out 100 times too big: c1 742.00 + 1758.00 = 2500.00. JNR_CUSTOMERS_ORDERS
(L3664) is a Master Outer Join with customers as master, so c3 (no orders) is dropped.
"""
import datetime as dt
from decimal import Decimal as D

import duckdb
import pytest

from pc2dbt.convert import convert_mapping
from pc2dbt.parse import parse_file
from tests.helpers import DEMO_XML, run_model

pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not DEMO_XML.exists(), reason="demo XML not cloned into external/")

STAGING = """
create table stg_customers (customer_id varchar, customer_name varchar);
insert into stg_customers values ('c1', 'Ann'), ('c2', 'Bob'), ('c3', 'Cat'), ('c4', 'Dan');
create table stg_orders (order_id varchar, customer_id varchar, location_id varchar, ordered_at_day timestamp,
    subtotal_cents decimal(15,0), tax_paid_cents decimal(15,0), order_total_cents decimal(12,2),
    subtotal decimal(15,0), tax_paid decimal(15,0), order_total decimal(12,2));
insert into stg_orders values
    ('o1', 'c1', 's1', '2024-09-01', 7, 0, 7.42, 700, 42, 742.00),
    ('o2', 'c1', 's1', '2025-01-31', 16, 2, 17.58, 1600, 158, 1758.00),
    ('o3', 'c2', 's1', '2025-02-01', 5, 0, 5.30, 500, 30, 530.00),
    ('o4', 'c2', 's1', '2024-06-01', 11, 1, 11.66, 1100, 66, 1166.00),
    ('o5', 'c4', 's1', '2025-04-01', 5, 0, 4.77, 450, 27, 477.00);
create table stg_order_items (order_item_id varchar, order_id varchar, product_id varchar);
insert into stg_order_items values ('i1', 'o1', 'JAF-001'), ('i2', 'o1', 'BEV-001'), ('i3', 'o2', 'JAF-001'),
    ('i4', 'o4', 'JAF-001'), ('i5', 'o5', 'BEV-001');
create table stg_products (product_id varchar, product_name varchar, product_type varchar,
    product_price_cents decimal(15,0), product_price decimal(12,2), product_description varchar,
    is_food_item decimal(1,0), is_drink_item decimal(1,0));
insert into stg_products values ('JAF-001', 'nutellaphone', 'jaffle', 11, 1100.00, 'warm', 1, 0),
    ('BEV-001', 'tea', 'beverage', 5, 450.00, 'hot', 0, 1);
create table stg_supplies (supply_id varchar, supply_name varchar, supply_cost_cents decimal(12,2),
    supply_cost decimal(12,2), is_perishable decimal(1,0), product_id varchar);
insert into stg_supplies values ('SUP-001', 'knife', 7.00, 0.07, 0, 'JAF-001'),
    ('SUP-002', 'cup', 30.00, 0.30, 0, 'BEV-001'), ('SUP-003', 'bread', 50.00, 0.50, 0, 'JAF-001');
"""


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def models():
    return {m.name: m for m in convert_mapping(parse_file(DEMO_XML), "m_FL_JS_MARTS_CORE")}


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def con():
    c = duckdb.connect()
    c.execute(STAGING)
    return c


def test_one_model_per_core_target(models):
    assert sorted(models) == ["customers", "order_items", "orders", "products", "supplies"]
    assert {m.folder for m in models.values()} == {"m_fl_js_marts_core"}


def test_orders_drops_orders_without_items_and_counts_across_customers(models, con):
    assert run_model(con, models["orders"].sql) == [
        ("o1", "c1", "s1", dt.datetime(2024, 9, 1), D("0.07"), D("0.00"), D("0.07"), D("1550.00"), D("0.87"), D("1"), D("1"), D("1")),
        ("o2", "c1", "s1", dt.datetime(2025, 1, 31), D("0.16"), D("0.02"), D("0.18"), D("1100.00"), D("0.57"), D("1"), D("0"), D("2")),
        ("o4", "c2", "s1", dt.datetime(2024, 6, 1), D("0.11"), D("0.01"), D("0.12"), D("1100.00"), D("0.57"), D("1"), D("0"), D("3")),
        ("o5", "c4", "s1", dt.datetime(2025, 4, 1), D("0.05"), D("0.00"), D("0.05"), D("450.00"), D("0.30"), D("0"), D("1"), D("4")),
    ]


def test_orders_flags_the_counter_its_sorter_and_both_master_outer_joins(models):
    flags = models["orders"].flags
    assert [f.line for f in flags if f.kind == "counter"] == [3589]
    assert [f.line for f in flags if f.kind == "sort_order"] == [3554]
    assert sorted(f.line for f in flags if f.kind == "master_outer") == [3446, 3519]


def test_customers_sums_cents_and_drops_customers_without_orders(models, con):
    assert run_model(con, models["customers"].sql) == [
        ("c1", "Ann", D("2"), dt.datetime(2024, 9, 1), dt.datetime(2025, 1, 31), D("2500.00"), D("2300.00"), D("200.00"), "returning"),
        ("c2", "Bob", D("2"), dt.datetime(2024, 6, 1), dt.datetime(2025, 2, 1), D("1696.00"), D("1600.00"), D("96.00"), "returning"),
        ("c4", "Dan", D("1"), dt.datetime(2025, 4, 1), dt.datetime(2025, 4, 1), D("477.00"), D("450.00"), D("27.00"), "new"),
    ]


def test_customers_flags_its_master_outer_join(models):
    assert [f.line for f in models["customers"].flags if f.kind == "master_outer"] == [3664]


def test_order_items_adds_product_and_supply_cost(models, con):
    # PRODUCT_PRICE comes from stg_products.product_price, which holds cents (swap at L621).
    jaffle = ("nutellaphone", "jaffle", D("1100.00"), D("1"), D("0"), D("0.57"), D("0"))
    tea = ("tea", "beverage", D("450.00"), D("0"), D("1"), D("0.30"), D("0"))
    assert run_model(con, models["order_items"].sql) == [
        ("i1", "o1", "JAF-001", dt.datetime(2024, 9, 1), *jaffle),
        ("i2", "o1", "BEV-001", dt.datetime(2024, 9, 1), *tea),
        ("i3", "o2", "JAF-001", dt.datetime(2025, 1, 31), *jaffle),
        ("i4", "o4", "JAF-001", dt.datetime(2024, 6, 1), *jaffle),
        ("i5", "o5", "BEV-001", dt.datetime(2025, 4, 1), *tea),
    ]
    assert [f.line for f in models["order_items"].flags if f.kind == "master_outer"] == [3319]


def test_products_and_supplies_pass_staging_through(models, con):
    assert run_model(con, models["products"].sql) == [
        ("BEV-001", "tea", "beverage", D("5"), D("450.00"), "hot", D("0"), D("1")),
        ("JAF-001", "nutellaphone", "jaffle", D("11"), D("1100.00"), "warm", D("1"), D("0"))]
    assert run_model(con, models["supplies"].sql) == [
        ("SUP-001", "knife", D("7.00"), D("0.07"), D("0"), "JAF-001"),
        ("SUP-002", "cup", D("30.00"), D("0.30"), D("0"), "BEV-001"),
        ("SUP-003", "bread", D("50.00"), D("0.50"), D("0"), "JAF-001")]

content.text:
I committed step 1 as `7e6ed3e` and then built step 2, the core marts. The core mapping converts to 5 more models and builds with dbt on DuckDB, with 0 unexplained differences from jaffle-shop. All 93 unit tests and 6 reference tests pass. Step 2 is not committed.

## Your question: I picked neither option exactly

Every column is now read with the name of the step it comes from, for example `sq_raw_orders.subtotal`. A name with its step in front can never mean an output of the same select, in any database. Why not your two options:
- **`subtotal_in` names:** they would fix `exp_orders`, but the target select has the same problem. `cast(subtotal_cents …) as subtotal` comes three lines after `… as subtotal_cents`. There the input names are the target's own column names, so `_in` names can't help.
- **Only a test:** that would pin DuckDB's rule, not the SQL. Instead, a new test parses every generated select with DuckDB's parser and fails if any column is read without its step's name. It failed on all 7 models before the change.

## The SQL for `EXP_CUSTOMER_ORDER_NUM`

The Sorter before it is kept as a step, because the counter needs its order. Flag text is shortened here; the full text is in `out/models/m_fl_js_marts_core/orders.sql`.

```sql
-- SRT_BY_CUSTOMER · Sorter · L3554–3575 · kept: its order numbers the rows for EXP_CUSTOMER_ORDER_NUM (decision Q12)
srt_by_customer as (
    select
        exp_orders_calc.customer_id,
        … 10 more columns passed through …
        row_number() over (
            order by lower(exp_orders_calc.customer_id) asc nulls first,
                     exp_orders_calc.ordered_at_day asc nulls first,
                     lower(exp_orders_calc.order_id) asc nulls first
        ) as sort_position  -- FLAG sort_order L3554: … case is ignored (L3567) … NULLs sort low (L3571)
    from exp_orders_calc
),

-- EXP_CUSTOMER_ORDER_NUM · Expression · L3576–3592
exp_customer_order_num as (
    select
        srt_by_customer.order_id,
        srt_by_customer.customer_id,
        srt_by_customer.location_id,
        srt_by_customer.ordered_at_day,
        srt_by_customer.subtotal_recal as subtotal,
        srt_by_customer.tax_paid_recal as tax_paid,
        srt_by_customer.order_total_recal as order_total,
        srt_by_customer.order_items_subtotal_cl as order_items_subtotal,
        srt_by_customer.order_cost_cl as order_cost,
        srt_by_customer.has_food_items_cl as has_food_items,
        srt_by_customer.has_drink_items_cl as has_drink_items,
        srt_by_customer.sort_position
            - coalesce(max(case when srt_by_customer.customer_id is null then srt_by_customer.sort_position end)
                       over (order by srt_by_customer.sort_position) - 1, 0) as customer_order_number
            -- FLAG counter L3589: v_PREV_CUSTOMER_ID is set to this row's CUSTOMER_ID (L3588) before the comparison …
    from srt_by_customer
)
```

- **Why one running number:** `v_PREV_CUSTOMER_ID` takes this row's `CUSTOMER_ID` (L3588) before `v_ORDER_SEQUENCE` compares them (L3589). So the comparison is true on every row, and the number never restarts per customer.
- **NULL customer:** `NULL = NULL` isn't true, so a row with no customer goes back to 1. That's what the `coalesce(max(…))` part copies.
- **Case and NULL settings:** the hand-made fixture has keys that differ only by case and two rows with no customer. Sorting case-sensitively, putting NULLs last, or numbering per customer each makes the test fail.
- **On the real data:** the number equals the row position, 1 to 61,465, on every row.
- **Anything else:** another variable-port pattern, or variable ports without a Sorter right before them, stops with a clear error (decision Q13).

## The SQL for `JNR_CUSTOMERS_ORDERS`

No box is called `jnr_customer_orders`; the closest is `JNR_CUSTOMERS_ORDERS` (L3651):

```sql
-- JNR_CUSTOMERS_ORDERS · Joiner · L3651–3673 · Master Outer Join
jnr_customers_orders as (
    select
        master.customer_id,
        master.customer_name,
        detail.lifetime_orders,
        detail.first_order_date,
        detail.last_order_date,
        detail.lifetime_spend,
        detail.lifetime_spend_pretax,
        detail.lifetime_tax_paid
    from agg_orders_by_customer as detail
    left join sq_stg_customers as master  -- FLAG master_outer L3664: keeps every row from AGG_ORDERS_BY_CUSTOMER (detail) and only
        on master.customer_id = detail.customer_id          -- the matching rows from SQ_STG_CUSTOMERS (master); unmatched customers are dropped
),
```

It drops customers who have no orders. On the seed data that's none, because all 935 customers have orders.

The 483 orders drop at a different join, `JNR_ORDERS_ITEMS_AGG` (L3519). There the per-order item totals are the kept side:

```sql
    from agg_items_by_order as detail
    left join sq_stg_orders1 as master  -- FLAG master_outer L3519: … SQ_STG_ORDERS1 rows with no match are dropped
        on master.order_id = detail.order_id
```

Right after that join, `jnr_orders_items_agg.subtotal_cents / 100` divides a column that holds dollars because of the staging swap. That's where the amounts become 100 times too small.

## Comparison with jaffle-shop (marts)

| Table | Rows (ours / jaffle-shop) | Match | Explained | Unexplained | Not compared |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| customers | 935 / 935 | 6 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| orders | 61,465 / 61,948 (483 explained) | 7 | 5 | 0 | 6 |
| order_items | 90,900 / 90,900 | 8 | 1 | 0 | 2 |
| products | 10 / 10 | 6 | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| supplies | 65 / 65 | 4 | 1 | 0 | 2 |

I checked every reason against the data:
- **The 483 missing orders** are exactly the orders with no items.
- **Order amounts:** subtotal is exactly 100 times too small on all 61,465 rows. Tax also loses its cents, and the total is rounded to 2 places.
- **Customer lifetime amounts** are exactly 100 times too big on all 935 customers. They sum the staging columns that hold cents.
- **Order items subtotal and product price** are 100 times too big, from the price swap at L621.
- **The counter** equals jaffle-shop's per-customer number on 190 of 61,465 rows, by chance.
- **`order_cost` matches exactly,** because supply costs never went through a swap.

Staging is unchanged: 23 columns match, 8 are explained and 0 are unexplained. The Results page now has a section per mapping and works at desktop and phone widths.

## Test results

- **Unit tests: 93 passed in about 1 second** (53 before step 2).
  - Fixture tests for the new box types: 8
  - The real core mapping on hand-made staging rows, with hand-worked values: 8
  - Aggregate functions: 8
  - The qualified-name check across 5 mappings: 15
  - Parser: 1
- **Reference tests (`pytest -m reference`): 6 passed,** 3 for staging and 3 for marts.

f = parse_file("external/flowline-pwc-demo/FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml")

    for t in m.transformations.values():
        ports = list(t.ports.values())
        vars_ = [p for p in ports if p.port_type == "LOCAL VARIABLE"]
        if not vars_:
            continue
        print(f"== {mname} {t.name} {t.type} L{t.line}-{t.end}")
        names = [p.name.upper() for p in ports]
        for i, p in enumerate(ports):
            if p.port_type != "LOCAL VARIABLE" and not any(re.search(rf"\b{v.name}\b", p.expression, re.I) for v in vars_):
                continue
            # variables this expression reads, and whether each is defined at or after this port (= previous row's value)
            reads = [v for v in vars_ if re.search(rf"\b{v.name}\b", p.expression, re.I)]
            later = [v.name for v in reads if ports.index(v) >= i]
            print(f"   L{p.line} {p.port_type:15} {p.name:26} = {p.expression}" + (f"   <-- reads previous row: {later}" if later else ""))

X=external/flowline-pwc-demo/FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml; sed -n 3104p $X | grep -oE '(NAME|DEFAULTVALUE|DATATYPE) ="[^"]*"' | paste -s -d' ' -; .venv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
from pc2dbt.parse import parse_file
f = parse_file("external/flowline-pwc-demo/FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml")
m = f.mappings["m_FL_JS_MARTS_ENRICHED"]
into = {(c.to_instance, c.to_field): c for c in m.connectors}
def trace(inst, port, depth=0):
    while True:
        t = m.transformations.get(m.instances[inst].definition) if m.instances[inst].type == "TRANSFORMATION" else None
        p = t.ports.get(port) if t else None
        info = f"{inst}.{port}" + (f" [{t.type}] = {p.expression!r}" if p and p.expression and p.expression.upper() != port.upper() else "")
        print("   " * depth + info)
        if t and t.type == "Router" and p and p.ref_field: port = p.ref_field
        if p and p.expression and p.expression.upper() != port.upper() and t.type != "Aggregator":
            return
        if t and t.type == "Aggregator" and p and p.expression and p.expression.upper() != port.upper():
            return
        c = into.get((inst, port))
        if c is None: return
        inst, port = c.from_instance, c.from_field
print("value band input:"); trace("RTR_ORDER_VALUE_BAND", "ORDER_TOTAL")
print("joins on the way (type, master, condition):")
for n in ("JNR_ITEMS_ORDERS", "JNR_ORDERS_ITEMS_AGG", "JNR_ADD_LOCATIONS", "JNR_ADD_LOCATION_INFO", "JNR_ADD_CUSTOMERS", "JNR_ADD_PRODUCTS", "JNR_ADD_SUPPLIES", "JNR_CUSTOMERS"):
    t = m.transformations[n]
    masters = sorted({into[(n, p.name)].from_instance for p in t.ports.values() if p.is_master and (n, p.name) in into})
    details = sorted({into[(n, p.name)].from_instance for p in t.ports.values() if not p.is_master and (n, p.name) in into})
    print(f"   {n} L{t.line}: {t.attr('Join Type')} | master {masters} | detail {details} | {t.attr('Join Condition')}")
fil = m.transformations["FIL_LOCS"]
print("FIL_LOCS condition:", fil.attr("Filter Condition"), "L", fil.attributes.get("Filter Condition", ("", 0))[1])
targets_of = lambda inst: sorted({c.to_instance for c in m.connectors if c.from_instance == inst})
for n in ("JNR_ADD_LOCATIONS", "JNR_ADD_LOCATION_INFO", "FIL_LOCS"):
    print(f"   {n} feeds {targets_of(n)}")
EOF
