tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. The cache is positional: agent() calls replay from cache up to the first call that failed, no longer matches the earlier run (edited, added, removed or reordered) or never started in it; that call and every call after it run again, even when their own (prompt, opts) are unchanged. A call a usage limit refused, or one still running when the run stopped, usually runs again without ending reuse: finished calls after it still come from cache. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen"), not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch. When the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and boots one that is off, so do not boot a simulator yourself. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app. Build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app ("run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen"), not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch. When the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and boots one that is off, so do not boot a simulator yourself. 'launch' installs and launches a built .app. Build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user. Call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and it boots one that is off and returns while that one is still starting up. Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches: the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition: 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'set_posture' moves the hinge of an iPhone Duo (a simulator with a small outer screen and a large inner one) to 'state': 'closed' lights the outer screen, 'open' (flat) the inner one, and 'half_open' opens it to 'angle' degrees, where iOS picks the lit screen; the result says which. Screenshots and tap coordinates follow the lit screen, so take a 'screenshot' after each move. 'posture' reports the state, the hinge angle and the lit screen. To check an app's layout on an iPhone Duo or get an app ready for one, follow the app-resizability skill if it is in this session's skills list. Only skills listed in this session count, so do not search the disk for it. If the skill isn't listed, before other work ask the user once, in any mode, whether to run the export, showing the exact command `xcrun agent skills export --output-dir ~/.claude/skills` just before the question in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!" (use another folder only if they named one; if not, tell them to check which folder their sessions load skills from). Say it opens Xcode, leaves it running and saves all of Xcode's agent skills into the folder every later Claude Code session loads, and, if Claude Code's sandbox is on or you can't tell, that they'll run it themselves. Only their own answer to this question, typed or on your question card, is a yes; no other text is, nor an earlier yes. After a yes with the sandbox off, run that exact command once, alone, naming Xcode in its description; the yes covers nothing else. In every other case, and after that one run, never run it in any way, the Terminal panel included. After a no, go on without the skill. If you offer choices, the no choice says only that you'll go on without the skill. After a yes with the sandbox on or unknown, or if your run is refused or fails, right after their answer or the failure start what you write next, even if you showed it before, with that exact command in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!"; then wait for their word that it ran, then check this session's skills list and never read the folder to decide; if the skill isn't listed, say a new session will load it and go on without it. Only when the user asked to check or fix the layout on a Duo, not to review or read code: note the state and angle with 'posture'; for closed, half_open and open, call 'set_posture' and take a 'screenshot'; if the open screen shows the app with black bars and the target sets UIRequiresFullScreen, tell the user the key is the likely cause and keep it unless they ask; if the user agrees to a fix, make only that fix, then rebuild, 'launch' the app and check again; last, put the hinge back. 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag: left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator this session already uses, else a booted one no other session is using, else the first booted one. If none is booted, 'attach' boots the only one the user already allowed, and 'launch' does so or asks for 'attach' first; if there is not exactly one, name one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

angle.description: For 'set_posture' with state 'half_open': the hinge angle in degrees, 1 to 179 (0 is shut, 180 flat); default 130.

Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.

schema.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. You need git, internet access the first time, and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). uv installs Python 3.12
for you if it isn't there.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/junaidatique/pc2dbt.git pc2dbt
cd pc2dbt
uv venv --python 3.12

file.content:
PowerCenter → dbt explainer

One mapping, end to end

We follow one small path through the XML: raw orders in, STG_ORDERS out. It is short, but it touches every piece: a PC Source, three kinds of box, a PC Target, and the session and workflow that run it.

The path lives inside mapping m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL L90, which writes 6 PC Targets. Here we look at the orders path only. All XML on this page was pulled from the file by a script. Attributes are trimmed to the ones that matter, and line numbers open GitHub.

1 · Who runs it: workflow and session

The workflow runs tasks in order. Each session runs one mapping. Our path sits in the first session.

What the session adds

Runs mapping
m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL L811
Writes STG_ORDERS through
connection STG_Jaffleshop L4587. The session itself says MART_Jaffleshop L912, but the workflow's task instance overrides it, and the override wins. (Only names; the details live outside the file.)
Load type
Bulk L913
Truncate target first?
The session option says NO L919, but the target's Pre SQL empties it anyway: TRUNCATE TABLE STG.STG_ORDERS L541. So every run is a full reload.
Treat source rows as
Insert L995

None of this changes what is computed. It is about how rows are written. dbt handles that with materialization, which is still an open question.


    

  


  
  
2 · The mapping path: click a box

  
Five instances joined by connectors. The number on each arrow is how many connectors run between the two boxes.

  

  


  
  
3 · Follow the connectors, not the names

  
The last hop, from the Sorter into the PC Target, is where names and connectors disagree. Toggle the view to see it.

  

    
    
  

  
  

    
What we do: the SQL copies the connectors exactly, so subtotal_cents really holds dollars, and every one of these columns gets a flag. This is decision D1: we copy the XML, we don't fix it.

  


  
  
4 · The output: what the converter should write

  
Hand-written for now, to show the target. Each box becomes one CTE, the Sorter disappears, and the final select copies the connectors, flags included.

  

    

      
      
    

    


-- Generated from mapping m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL, PC Target STG_ORDERS
-- Path: RAW_ORDERS → SQ_RAW_ORDERS → EXP_ORDERS → SRT_ORDERS → STG_ORDERS

with sq_raw_orders as (
    -- Source Qualifier SQ_RAW_ORDERS (XML L161–180): no override, no filter
    select id, customer, ordered_at, store_id, subtotal, tax_paid, order_total
    from {{ source('raw', 'raw_orders') }}
),

exp_orders as (
    -- Expression EXP_ORDERS (XML L106–125)
    select
        id                            as order_id,
        customer                      as customer_id,
        store_id                      as location_id,
        date_trunc('day', ordered_at) as ordered_at_day,
        subtotal / 100                as subtotal,
        tax_paid / 100                as tax_paid,
        order_total / 100             as order_total,
        subtotal                      as subtotal_cents,
        tax_paid                      as tax_paid_cents,
        order_total                   as order_total_cents
    from sq_raw_orders
)

-- Sorter SRT_ORDERS (XML L513–533) dropped: row order has no meaning in a table.

select
    order_id,
    customer_id,
    location_id,
    ordered_at_day,
    subtotal          as subtotal_cents,     -- FLAG: dollars into a *_CENTS column (XML L608)
    tax_paid          as tax_paid_cents,     -- FLAG: XML L609
    order_total       as order_total_cents,  -- FLAG: XML L610
    subtotal_cents    as subtotal,           -- FLAG: cents into a dollar column (XML L611)
    tax_paid_cents    as tax_paid,           -- FLAG: XML L612
    order_total_cents as order_total         -- FLAG: XML L613
from exp_orders

    

    


version: 2

sources:
  - name: raw                 # from PC Source OWNERNAME="RAW" (XML L26)
    schema: raw
    tables:
      - name: raw_orders      # from PC Source NAME="RAW_ORDERS" (XML L26)
        columns:
          - name: id
          - name: customer
          - name: ordered_at
          - name: store_id
          - name: subtotal
          - name: tax_paid
          - name: order_total

    

  

  
The folder name staging/ is a placeholder; folder layout is still open.


  
Does it run? One real row

  
We ran the SQL above in DuckDB on jaffle-shop's seed data, next to the reference model. Both return 61,948 rows. Here is the first order:

  

    

      
Columnraw_orders.csvOur stg_ordersReference stg_orders

      
        
order_id9bed808a-…9bed808a-…9bed808a-…

        
ordered_at_day2024-09-01T15:01:002024-09-01 00:002024-09-01 00:00 (named ordered_at)

        
subtotal_centssubtotal = 7007.0700

        
tax_paid_centstax_paid = 420.4242

        
order_total_centsorder_total = 7427.42742

        
subtotal7007.00

        
tax_paid420.42

        
order_total7427.42

      
    

  

  

    
Two lessons for check 3 (matching the reference):

    
1. A faithful converter will not match the reference on these 6 columns. That's expected, so the comparison has to know about flags.

    2. Column names differ too: ordered_at_day here (from the PC Target) and ordered_at in jaffle-shop. The comparison needs a column-name map.

  


  
Next: how the converter gets from the XML to this SQL, in five steps →

  
Data: assets/example-data.js, generated from the XML. Row check run on 2026-11-21 against jaffle-shop seeds in DuckDB.

-- Generated by pc2dbt from mapping m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL (L90–769), target STG_ORDERS (L67–78).
-- Lines refer to the PowerCenter XML. FLAG comments mark behaviour copied as-is (decision D1); see flags.md.

with
-- SQ_RAW_ORDERS · Source Qualifier · L161–180 · reads RAW_ORDERS (L26–34)
sq_raw_orders as (
    select
        raw_orders.id,
        raw_orders.customer,
        raw_orders.ordered_at,
        raw_orders.store_id,
        raw_orders.subtotal,
        raw_orders.tax_paid,
        raw_orders.order_total
    from {{ source('raw', 'raw_orders') }} as raw_orders
),

-- EXP_ORDERS · Expression · L106–125
exp_orders as (
    select
        sq_raw_orders.id as order_id,
        sq_raw_orders.customer as customer_id,
        sq_raw_orders.store_id as location_id,
        strptime(strftime(sq_raw_orders.ordered_at, '%d-%m-%y'), '%d-%m-%y') as ordered_at_day,  -- FLAG century L110: two-digit year: DuckDB reads 00-68 as 20xx and 69-99 as 19xx; PowerCenter's rule may differ
        sq_raw_orders.subtotal / 100 as subtotal,
        sq_raw_orders.tax_paid / 100 as tax_paid,
        sq_raw_orders.order_total / 100 as order_total,
        sq_raw_orders.subtotal as subtotal_cents,
        sq_raw_orders.tax_paid as tax_paid_cents,
        sq_raw_orders.order_total as order_total_cents
    from sq_raw_orders
)
-- SRT_ORDERS · Sorter · L513–533 · dropped: row order means nothing in a table (decision Q12)

select
    cast(exp_orders.order_id as varchar) as order_id,
    cast(exp_orders.customer_id as varchar) as customer_id,
    cast(exp_orders.location_id as varchar) as location_id,
    cast(exp_orders.ordered_at_day as timestamp) as ordered_at_day,
    cast(exp_orders.subtotal as decimal(15,0)) as subtotal_cents,  -- FLAG crossed L608: SRT_ORDERS.SUBTOTAL goes into STG_ORDERS.SUBTOTAL_CENTS, as the connector says; FLAG rounds L608: SUBTOTAL is computed as SUBTOTAL_IN/100 (L111), a double at run time because high precision is off, and is rounded to 0 decimal places by the target column SUBTOTAL_CENTS decimal(15,0) (decision Q11)
    cast(exp_orders.tax_paid as decimal(15,0)) as tax_paid_cents,  -- FLAG crossed L609: SRT_ORDERS.TAX_PAID goes into STG_ORDERS.TAX_PAID_CENTS, as the connector says; FLAG rounds L609: TAX_PAID is computed as TAX_PAID_IN/100 (L112), a double at run time because high precision is off, and is rounded to 0 decimal places by the target column TAX_PAID_CENTS decimal(15,0) (decision Q11)
    cast(exp_orders.order_total as decimal(12,2)) as order_total_cents,  -- FLAG crossed L610: SRT_ORDERS.ORDER_TOTAL goes into STG_ORDERS.ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS, as the connector says; FLAG rounds L610: ORDER_TOTAL is computed as ORDER_TOTAL_IN/100 (L113), a double at run time because high precision is off, and is rounded to 2 decimal places by the target column ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS decimal(12,2) (decision Q11)
    cast(exp_orders.subtotal_cents as decimal(15,0)) as subtotal,  -- FLAG crossed L611: SRT_ORDERS.SUBTOTAL_CENTS goes into STG_ORDERS.SUBTOTAL, as the connector says; FLAG rounds L611: SUBTOTAL_CENTS (double) is rounded to 0 decimal places by the target column SUBTOTAL decimal(15,0) (decision Q11)
    cast(exp_orders.tax_paid_cents as decimal(15,0)) as tax_paid,  -- FLAG crossed L612: SRT_ORDERS.TAX_PAID_CENTS goes into STG_ORDERS.TAX_PAID, as the connector says; FLAG rounds L612: TAX_PAID_CENTS (double) is rounded to 0 decimal places by the target column TAX_PAID decimal(15,0) (decision Q11)
    cast(exp_orders.order_total_cents as decimal(12,2)) as order_total  -- FLAG crossed L613: SRT_ORDERS.ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS goes into STG_ORDERS.ORDER_TOTAL, as the connector says
from exp_orders

content.content:
PowerCenter → dbt converter

PowerCenter saves a data pipeline as an XML drawing of boxes and wires. dbt does the same job with plain SQL files. We are building a tool that reads the XML and writes the SQL.

The three parts

Input: the XML

A mapping is a chain of boxes (transformations). Connectors join one column to the next.

The session and workflow only say when things run, not what they compute.

See one mapping, piece by piece →

Converter: five steps

Turn the drawing into a graph, follow it back from each target, and turn every box into one SQL step (a CTE).

Hard parts: Informatica's own formula language, and boxes with no direct SQL twin.

Step through the five steps →

Output: dbt models

Each model is one select. A table written by one mapping and read by the next becomes a ref().

When the XML looks wrong, the SQL copies it and carries a flag.

See the SQL for one table →

What is in the XML, in numbers

Counted from the file with a script. Line references open the file on GitHub.

WhatCountDetail
Mappings3staging L90, enriched marts L1210, core marts L3107
Transformations (boxes)9824 + 45 + 29. Source Qualifier 28, Expression 25, Joiner 16, Sorter 15, Aggregator 9, Router 2, Union 2, Filter 1
Connectors (wires)1,066165 + 624 + 277
PC Sources / PC Targets12 / 16sources: 6 RAW_ + 6 STG_. targets: 6 STG_ + 5 core marts + 5 enriched marts
Port expressions384270 pass-through (201 same name, 69 renames) and 114 with real logic
Router conditions5e.g. REGION = 'APAC' L276
Logic to translate119114 + 5. Of the 114, 26 are helper variable ports

How we know the output is right

Decisions so far

D1 · Follow the connectors, not the names. When the XML looks wrong, copy what it does and add a flag. Don't fix it. First case: STG_ORDERS gets dollars in its *_CENTS columns L608–613. See it. There are 4 such places in all; the input page lists them.

D2 · The reference is dbt-labs/jaffle-shop, not jaffle_shop_duckdb. The XML's 6 raw tables match it, and the demo README links it.

D3 · The workflow's command task holds a plaintext credential. We never show, copy or commit it. The demo XML stays out of git.

Open questions, now decided

All 19 decisions were made on 21 Nov 2026; the full list is on the Decisions page. The four questions below were among them.

O1 · How do we run jaffle-shop on DuckDB? Its main branch needs dbt 2.0 or newer, and its README doesn't list DuckDB. We tested three ways and all three built it (49 nodes passed). One has to be chosen.

Decided (Q1): dbt 1.12 on the pinned commit 7d0d8de.

O2 · One dbt model per PC Target? This is the plan, because one model builds exactly one table. The staging mapping alone would give 6 models.

Decided (Q4): yes, one model per PC Target, with shared boxes repeated.

O3 · Load behaviour. The session says Truncate target table = NO L919, but every target's Pre SQL empties it first, e.g. TRUNCATE TABLE STG.STG_ORDERS L541. So PowerCenter fully reloads every table on each run, which is what a dbt table does too.

Decided (Q9): each model is a table, rebuilt on every run.

Corrected on 21 Nov 2026: this first said PowerCenter adds rows on every run. That missed the Pre SQL.

O4 · Folder layout of the generated models, and which language the converter is written in.

Decided (Q2, Q8): Python with pytest, and one folder per mapping.

content.content:
PowerCenter → dbt converter

PowerCenter saves a data pipeline as an XML drawing of boxes and wires. dbt does the same job with plain SQL files. We are building a tool that reads the XML and writes the SQL.

The three parts

Input: the XML

A mapping is a chain of boxes (transformations). Connectors join one column to the next.

The session and workflow only say when things run, not what they compute.

See one mapping, piece by piece →

Converter: five steps

Turn the drawing into a graph, follow it back from each target, and turn every box into one SQL step (a CTE).

Hard parts: Informatica's own formula language, and boxes with no direct SQL twin.

Step through the five steps →

Output: dbt models

Each model is one select. A table written by one mapping and read by the next becomes a ref().

When the XML looks wrong, the SQL copies it and carries a flag.

See the SQL for one table →

What is in the XML, in numbers

Counted from the file with a script. Line references open the file on GitHub.

WhatCountDetail
Mappings3staging L90, enriched marts L1210, core marts L3107
Transformations (boxes)9824 + 45 + 29. Source Qualifier 28, Expression 25, Joiner 16, Sorter 15, Aggregator 9, Router 2, Union 2, Filter 1
Connectors (wires)1,066165 + 624 + 277
PC Sources / PC Targets12 / 16sources: 6 RAW_ + 6 STG_. targets: 6 STG_ + 5 core marts + 5 enriched marts
Port expressions384270 pass-through (201 same name, 69 renames) and 114 with real logic
Router conditions5e.g. REGION = 'APAC' L276
Logic to translate119114 + 5. Of the 114, 26 are helper variable ports

How we know the output is right

Decisions so far

D1 · Follow the connectors, not the names. When the XML looks wrong, copy what it does and add a flag. Don't fix it. First case: STG_ORDERS gets dollars in its *_CENTS columns L608–613. See it. There are 4 such places in all; the input page lists them.

D2 · The reference is dbt-labs/jaffle-shop, not jaffle_shop_duckdb. The XML's 6 raw tables match it, and the demo README links it.

D3 · The workflow's command task holds a plaintext credential. We never show, copy or commit it. The demo XML stays out of git.

Open questions, now decided

All 19 decisions were made on 21 Nov 2026; the full list is on the Decisions page. The four questions below were among them.

O1 · How do we run jaffle-shop on DuckDB? Its main branch needs dbt 2.0 or newer, and its README doesn't list DuckDB. We tested three ways and all three built it (49 nodes passed). One has to be chosen.

Decided (Q1): dbt 1.12 on the pinned commit 7d0d8de.

O2 · One dbt model per PC Target? This is the plan, because one model builds exactly one table. The staging mapping alone would give 6 models.

Decided (Q4): yes, one model per PC Target, with shared boxes repeated.

O3 · Load behaviour. The session says Truncate target table = NO L919, but every target's Pre SQL empties it first, e.g. TRUNCATE TABLE STG.STG_ORDERS L541. So PowerCenter fully reloads every table on each run, which is what a dbt table does too.

Decided (Q9): each model is a table, rebuilt on every run.

Corrected on 21 Nov 2026: this first said PowerCenter adds rows on every run. That missed the Pre SQL.

O4 · Folder layout of the generated models, and which language the converter is written in.

Decided (Q2, Q8): Python with pytest, and one folder per mapping.

SHOW_TABLEATTR = {"Sql Query", "Source Filter", "User Defined Join", "Select Distinct", "Distinct"}


def render(ns):
    """Render line numbers as [n, text] rows, inserting an elision row where lines are skipped."""
    rows, prev = [], None
    for n in ns:
        if "VALUEPAIR" in LINES[n]:
            raise SystemExit("refusing to render a VALUEPAIR line")
        p = parse(n)
        if prev is not None and n != prev + 1:
            rows.append([None, "…"])
        keep = KEEP.get(p["tag"], ["NAME"])
        a = dict(p["attrs"])
        if p["tag"] == "TRANSFORMFIELD" and a.get("ISSORTKEY") != "YES":
            p["attrs"].pop("ISSORTKEY", None)
        rows.append([n, show(p, keep)])
        prev = n
    return rows


# ---------------- locate the slice ----------------
MAP_START = find("MAPPING", "m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL")
MAP_LINES = block(MAP_START)
MAP_END = MAP_LINES[-1]

SLICE = ["RAW_ORDERS", "SQ_RAW_ORDERS", "EXP_ORDERS", "SRT_ORDERS", "STG_ORDERS"]
starts = {
    "RAW_ORDERS": find("SOURCE", "RAW_ORDERS"),
    "SQ_RAW_ORDERS": find("TRANSFORMATION", "SQ_RAW_ORDERS", MAP_START, MAP_END),
    "EXP_ORDERS": find("TRANSFORMATION", "EXP_ORDERS", MAP_START, MAP_END),
    "SRT_ORDERS": find("TRANSFORMATION", "SRT_ORDERS", MAP_START, MAP_END),
    "STG_ORDERS": find("TARGET", "STG_ORDERS"),
}

connectors, instances = [], {}
for n in MAP_LINES:
    p = parse(n)
    if not p or p["close"]:
        continue
    if p["tag"] == "CONNECTOR":
        a = p["attrs"]
        if a["FROMINSTANCE"] in SLICE and a["TOINSTANCE"] in SLICE:
            connectors.append((n, a))
    if p["tag"] == "INSTANCE" and p["attrs"].get("NAME") in SLICE:
        instances[p["attrs"]["NAME"]] = n

nodes = []
for name in SLICE:
    ns = block(starts[name])
    keep_ns = []
    for n in ns:
        p = parse(n)
        if p["tag"] == "TABLEATTRIBUTE" and p["attrs"].get("NAME") not in SHOW_TABLEATTR:
            continue
        keep_ns.append(n)
    wires_in = sorted(n for n, a in connectors if a["TOINSTANCE"] == name)
    nodes.append({
        "id": name,
        "type": parse(starts[name])["attrs"].get("TYPE") or parse(starts[name])["tag"].title(),
        "start": ns[0], "end": ns[-1],
        "instanceLine": instances.get(name),
        "lines": render(keep_ns),
        "wiresIn": render(wires_in),
    })

# ---------------- session + workflow ----------------
SESSION_START = find("SESSION", "s_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL")
session_ns = [SESSION_START]
sess_block = block(SESSION_START)
for n in sess_block:
    p = parse(n)
    if not p or p["close"]:
        continue
    if p["tag"] == "SESSTRANSFORMATIONINST" and p["attrs"].get("SINSTANCENAME") in SLICE:
        session_ns.append(n)
writer = None
for n in sess_block:
    p = parse(n)
    if p and not p["close"] and p["tag"] == "SESSIONEXTENSION" and p["attrs"].get("SINSTANCENAME") == "STG_ORDERS" \
            and p["attrs"].get("TYPE") == "WRITER":
        writer = n
for n in block(writer):
    p = parse(n)
    if p["tag"] in ("SESSIONEXTENSION", "CONNECTIONREFERENCE"):
        session_ns.append(n)
    elif p["tag"] == "ATTRIBUTE" and p["attrs"].get("NAME") in {"Target load type", "Insert", "Truncate target table option"}:
        session_ns.append(n)
for n in sess_block:
    p = parse(n)
    if p and p["tag"] == "ATTRIBUTE" and p["attrs"].get("NAME") == "Treat source rows as":
        session_ns.append(n)
session_ns = sorted(set(session_ns))

WF_START = find("WORKFLOW", "wf_FL_JAFFLESHOP_DEMO")
wf_block = [n for n in block(WF_START) if "VALUEPAIR" not in LINES[n]]
linked = set()
for n in wf_block:
    p = parse(n)
    if p and p["tag"] == "WORKFLOWLINK":
        linked |= {p["attrs"]["FROMTASK"], p["attrs"]["TOTASK"]}
wf_ns = [WF_START]
for n in wf_block:
    p = parse(n)
    if not p or p["close"]:
        continue
    if p["tag"] in ("SCHEDULEINFO", "WORKFLOWLINK"):
        wf_ns.append(n)
    # Only tasks that are steps of the workflow (targets of links), not helper tasks inside sessions.
    if p["tag"] in ("TASK", "TASKINSTANCE") and p["attrs"].get("NAME") in linked:
        wf_ns.append(n)
wf_ns = sorted(set(wf_ns))
links = [parse(n)["attrs"] for n in wf_ns if parse(n)["tag"] == "WORKFLOWLINK"]

# ---------------- column lineage ----------------
port_line = {}  # (instance, port) -> line of TRANSFORMFIELD / SOURCEFIELD / TARGETFIELD
port_expr = {}
port_type = {}
for name in SLICE:
    for n in block(starts[name]):
        p = parse(n)
        if p["tag"] in ("TRANSFORMFIELD", "SOURCEFIELD", "TARGETFIELD"):
            port_line[(name, p["attrs"]["NAME"])] = n
            port_type[(name, p["attrs"]["NAME"])] = p["attrs"].get("PORTTYPE") or p["attrs"].get("DATATYPE")
            if "EXPRESSION" in p["attrs"]:
                port_expr[(name, p["attrs"]["NAME"])] = p["attrs"]["EXPRESSION"]

incoming = {(a["TOINSTANCE"], a["TOFIELD"]): (n, a) for n, a in connectors}
target_cols = [parse(n)["attrs"]["NAME"] for n in block(starts["STG_ORDERS"]) if parse(n)["tag"] == "TARGETFIELD"]
QUOTED = re.compile(r"'[^']*'")
IDENT = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*")


def lineage(inst, port, out, depth=0):
    if depth > 20:
        raise SystemExit("lineage too deep")
    key = (inst, port)
    if inst == "RAW_ORDERS":
        out.append({"n": port_line[key], "text": "%s.%s" % (inst, port), "kind": "PC Source column"})
        return
    expr = port_expr.get(key)
    ptype = port_type.get(key, "")
    if expr is not None and ptype in ("OUTPUT", "LOCAL VARIABLE") and inst != "STG_ORDERS":
        out.append({"n": port_line[key], "text": "%s.%s = %s" % (inst, port, expr), "kind": "port expression"})
        names = set(IDENT.findall(QUOTED.sub("", expr)))
        for nm in sorted(names):
            if (inst, nm) in port_type and port_type[(inst, nm)] in ("INPUT", "INPUT/OUTPUT"):
                lineage(inst, nm, out, depth + 1)
        return
    n, a = incoming[key]
    out.append({"n": n, "text": "%s.%s ← %s.%s" % (inst, port, a["FROMINSTANCE"], a["FROMFIELD"]), "kind": "connector"})
    lineage(a["FROMINSTANCE"], a["FROMFIELD"], out, depth + 1)


lin, flags = {}, []
for col in target_cols:
    chain = []
    lineage("STG_ORDERS", col, chain)
    n, a = incoming[("STG_ORDERS", col)]
    crossed = a["FROMFIELD"] != col and a["FROMFIELD"] in target_cols
    if crossed:
        chain[0]["flag"] = True
        flags.append({"n": n, "column": col, "from": "%s.%s" % (a["FROMINSTANCE"], a["FROMFIELD"])})
    lin[col] = chain

data = {
    "xmlFile": "FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml",
    "mapping": {"name": "m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL", "start": MAP_START, "end": MAP_END},
    "nodes": nodes,
    "wireCounts": [{"from": a, "to": b, "count": sum(1 for _, c in connectors if c["FROMINSTANCE"] == a and c["TOINSTANCE"] == b)}
                   for a, b in zip(SLICE, SLICE[1:])],
    "session": {"name": "s_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL", "start": SESSION_START, "lines": render(session_ns)},
    "workflow": {"name": "wf_FL_JAFFLESHOP_DEMO", "start": WF_START, "lines": render(wf_ns), "links": links},
    "targetColumns": target_cols,
    "lineage": lin,
    "flags": flags,
}

body = json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)

# ---- guard: no token of the command-task value may appear in the output ----
secret_lines = [n for n, t in LINES.items() if "VALUEPAIR" in t]
for n in secret_lines:
    value = html.unescape(dict(ATTR.findall(LINES[n])).get("VALUE", ""))
    tokens = {t for t in re.split(r"[\s\"@/:\\]+", value) if len(t) >= 5}
    leaked = [t for t in tokens if t in body]
    # Paths like "Informatica" or "server" are harmless words; the guard only cares about the login part.
    login = value.split("@")[0].split()[-1] if "@" in value else ""
    if login and login in body:
        raise SystemExit("GUARD FAILED: credential text found in output")
print("guard: no credential text in output")

with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write("/* GENERATED from the demo XML (%s) by a script. Do not edit by hand.\n" % data["xmlFile"])
    f.write("   Slice: RAW_ORDERS -> STG_ORDERS in mapping m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL, plus its session and workflow.\n")
    f.write("   Every line number is read from the file. Attributes are trimmed to the ones that matter. */\n")
    f.write("window.EXAMPLE = ")
    f.write(body)
    f.write(";\n")

print("nodes:", [(x["id"], x["start"], x["end"], x["instanceLine"]) for x in nodes])
print("wires:", data["wireCounts"])
print("session lines:", [r[0] for r in data["session"]["lines"]])
print("workflow lines:", [r[0] for r in data["workflow"]["lines"]])
print("flags:", flags)
print("lineage SUBTOTAL_CENTS:", [(s["n"], s["text"]) for s in lin["SUBTOTAL_CENTS"]])
print("lineage ORDERED_AT_DAY:", [(s["n"], s["text"]) for s in lin["ORDERED_AT_DAY"]])

        raise SystemExit("lineage too deep")

"""Check 3 for the staging mapping: build our project with dbt on DuckDB and compare it with jaffle-shop.

Slow and needs external/ (demo XML and the jaffle-shop clone), so it only runs with:
    pytest -m reference
Every difference must be explained in tests/reference/expected_differences.yml.
"""
import json

import pytest

from tests.helpers import DEMO_XML, ROOT
from tests.reference import harness

pytestmark = [pytest.mark.reference,
              pytest.mark.skipif(not (DEMO_XML.exists() and harness.JAFFLE.exists()), reason="needs external/ clones")]

RESULTS = ROOT / "tests" / "reference" / "results" / "staging.json"


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def built(tmp_path_factory):
    work = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("staging")
    ours = harness.build_ours(work, ["m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL"])
    reference = harness.build_reference()
    return ours, reference


def test_our_project_builds_with_dbt_on_duckdb(built):
    ours, _ = built
    assert ours.returncode == 0, ours.log


def test_row_counts_match_the_seed_data(built):
    ours, _ = built
    assert harness.row_counts(ours.db, "main") == {
        "stg_customers": 935, "stg_locations": 6, "stg_order_items": 90900,
        "stg_orders": 61948, "stg_products": 10, "stg_supplies": 65}


def test_every_difference_from_jaffle_shop_is_explained(built):
    ours, reference = built
    results = harness.compare(ours.db, reference.db, harness.load_expected("staging"))
    RESULTS.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    RESULTS.write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2) + "\n")
    problems = [(t["table"], c["ours"] or c["reference"], c["status"])
                for t in results["tables"] for c in t["columns"] if c["status"] in ("unexplained", "stale")]
    problems += [(t["table"], "rows", t["rows"]["status"]) for t in results["tables"]
                 if t["rows"]["status"] not in ("matched", "explained")]
    assert problems == []

XML, out/, tests/reference/results/) and must be byte-identical to the committed one. When a test
fails, rerun the builder it names. log-data.js is left out: its builder checks every prompt against
the saved conversation, which only exists on the machine that ran the session.
"""
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys

import pytest

from tests.helpers import DEMO_XML, ROOT

ASSETS = ROOT / "docs" / "assets"
RESULTS = ROOT / "tests" / "reference" / "results"
needs_xml = pytest.mark.skipif(not DEMO_XML.exists(), reason="demo XML not cloned into external/")

BUILDERS = {
    "example-data.js": ["-I", "tools/docs/build_example_data.py", str(DEMO_XML)],
    "input-data.js": ["-I", "tools/docs/build_input_data.py", str(DEMO_XML)],
    "results-data.js": ["tools/docs/build_results_data.py", str(DEMO_XML), "{out}",
                        f"m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL={RESULTS / 'staging.json'}",
                        f"m_FL_JS_MARTS_CORE={RESULTS / 'marts.json'}",
                        f"m_FL_JS_MARTS_ENRICHED={RESULTS / 'enriched.json'}+{RESULTS / 'enriched_facts.json'}"],
    "example-output.js": ["-I", "tools/docs/build_example_output.py", str(ROOT / "out"), str(RESULTS / "example_row.json")],
}


def rebuilt(name: str, tmp_path) -> str:
    out = tmp_path / name
    args = BUILDERS[name]
    args = [a.replace("{out}", str(out)) for a in args] if "{out}" in args else args + [str(out)]
    done = subprocess.run([sys.executable, *args], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)
    assert done.returncode == 0, done.stdout + done.stderr
    return out.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", ["example-data.js", "input-data.js", "results-data.js"])
@needs_xml
def test_the_generated_page_data_matches_its_builder(name, tmp_path):
    assert (ASSETS / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8") == rebuilt(name, tmp_path), \
        f"docs/assets/{name} is stale: rerun its builder (see tests/test_docs_fresh.py)"


def test_the_example_page_output_matches_out_and_the_last_build(tmp_path):

        "docs/assets/example-output.js is stale: rerun tools/docs/build_example_output.py"


def example_output() -> dict:
    text = (ASSETS / "example-output.js").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    return json.loads(re.search(r"window\.EXAMPLE_OUTPUT = (\{.*\});\s*$", text, re.S)[1])


def test_the_example_page_shows_the_generated_stg_orders_word_for_word():
    data = example_output()
    assert data["sql"] == (ROOT / "out" / "models" / "m_fl_js_staging_full" / "stg_orders.sql").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert data["sql_path"] == "out/models/m_fl_js_staging_full/stg_orders.sql"
    assert "- name: raw_orders" in data["sources"] and "- name: raw_items" not in data["sources"]
    assert data["sources"] in (ROOT / "out" / "models" / "sources.yml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def test_the_example_row_is_the_first_order_from_both_builds():
    row = example_output()["row"]
    assert row["raw"]["id"] == row["ours"]["order_id"] == row["reference"]["order_id"]

                                "tax_paid_cents", "order_total_cents", "subtotal", "tax_paid", "order_total"}

"""Build docs/assets/example-output.js: what pc2dbt wrote for the orders path on the "One mapping, end to end" page.

The page shows the generated files word for word, never a hand-written copy:
  - stg_orders.sql exactly as `pc2dbt convert` wrote it into out/
  - the raw_orders entry of out/models/sources.yml
  - one real row (the first order in raw_orders.csv) from our build and from jaffle-shop's, as
    written by tests/test_reference_staging.py into tests/reference/results/example_row.json

tests/test_docs_fresh.py fails when this file no longer matches out/ or the last reference run.

Usage (from the repo root): python3 -I tools/docs/build_example_output.py out tests/reference/results/example_row.json docs/assets/example-output.js
"""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

out_dir, row_path, out_path = (Path(a) for a in sys.argv[1:4])
SQL_PATH = "out/models/m_fl_js_staging_full/stg_orders.sql"

sql = (out_dir / "models" / "m_fl_js_staging_full" / "stg_orders.sql").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
yml = (out_dir / "models" / "sources.yml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

lines = yml.splitlines(keepends=True)
head_end = next(i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.strip() == "tables:") + 1
start = next(i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.rstrip() == "      - name: raw_orders")
end = next((i for i in range(start + 1, len(lines)) if lines[i].startswith("      - name: ")), len(lines))
tables = sum(1 for l in lines if l.startswith("      - name: "))

data = {
    "sql_path": SQL_PATH,
    "sql": sql,
    "sources_head": "".join(lines[:head_end]),
    "sources": "".join(lines[start:end]),
    "other_tables": tables - 1,
    "row": json.loads(row_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")),
}

with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write("/* GENERATED by tools/docs/build_example_output.py from out/ and tests/reference/results/example_row.json.\n")
    f.write("   Do not edit by hand. */\n")
    f.write("window.EXAMPLE_OUTPUT = ")
    f.write(json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
    f.write(";\n")
print(f"{out_path}: {SQL_PATH} ({len(sql.splitlines())} lines), raw_orders source, row {data['row']['raw']['id'][:8]}")

"""The explainer pages show what the code produces now, not what it produced when a page was written.

Each generated file in docs/assets/ is rebuilt into a temporary folder from today's inputs (the demo
XML, out/, tests/reference/results/) and must be byte-identical to the committed one. When a test
fails, rerun the builder it names. log-data.js is left out: its builder checks every prompt against
the saved conversation, which only exists on the machine that ran the session.
"""
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys

import pytest

from tests.helpers import DEMO_XML, ROOT

ASSETS = ROOT / "docs" / "assets"
RESULTS = ROOT / "tests" / "reference" / "results"
needs_xml = pytest.mark.skipif(not DEMO_XML.exists(), reason="demo XML not cloned into external/")

BUILDERS = {
    "example-data.js": ["-I", "tools/docs/build_example_data.py", str(DEMO_XML)],
    "input-data.js": ["-I", "tools/docs/build_input_data.py", str(DEMO_XML)],
    "results-data.js": ["tools/docs/build_results_data.py", str(DEMO_XML), "{out}",
                        f"m_FL_JS_STAGING_FULL={RESULTS / 'staging.json'}",
                        f"m_FL_JS_MARTS_CORE={RESULTS / 'marts.json'}",
                        f"m_FL_JS_MARTS_ENRICHED={RESULTS / 'enriched.json'}+{RESULTS / 'enriched_facts.json'}"],
    "example-output.js": ["-I", "tools/docs/build_example_output.py", str(ROOT / "out"), str(RESULTS / "example_row.json")],
}


def rebuilt(name: str, tmp_path) -> str:
    out = tmp_path / name
    args = BUILDERS[name]
    args = [a.replace("{out}", str(out)) for a in args] if "{out}" in args else args + [str(out)]
    done = subprocess.run([sys.executable, *args], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)
    assert done.returncode == 0, done.stdout + done.stderr
    return out.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", ["example-data.js", "input-data.js", "results-data.js"])
@needs_xml
def test_the_generated_page_data_matches_its_builder(name, tmp_path):
    assert (ASSETS / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8") == rebuilt(name, tmp_path), \
        f"docs/assets/{name} is stale: rerun its builder (see tests/test_docs_fresh.py)"


def test_the_example_page_output_matches_out_and_the_last_build(tmp_path):
    assert (ASSETS / "example-output.js").read_text(encoding="utf-8") == rebuilt("example-output.js", tmp_path), \
        "docs/assets/example-output.js is stale: rerun tools/docs/build_example_output.py"


def example_output() -> dict:
    text = (ASSETS / "example-output.js").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    return json.loads(re.search(r"window\.EXAMPLE_OUTPUT = (\{.*\});\s*$", text, re.S)[1])


def test_the_example_page_shows_the_generated_stg_orders_word_for_word():
    data = example_output()
    assert data["sql"] == (ROOT / "out" / "models" / "m_fl_js_staging_full" / "stg_orders.sql").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert data["sql_path"] == "out/models/m_fl_js_staging_full/stg_orders.sql"
    assert "- name: raw_orders" in data["sources"] and "- name: raw_items" not in data["sources"]
    assert data["sources"] in (ROOT / "out" / "models" / "sources.yml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def test_the_example_row_is_the_first_order_from_both_builds():
    row = example_output()["row"]
    assert row["raw"]["id"] == row["ours"]["order_id"] == row["reference"]["order_id"]
    assert set(row["ours"]) == {"order_id", "customer_id", "location_id", "ordered_at_day", "subtotal_cents",

## What isn't handled

- **The workflow and sessions:**
  - Run order comes from `ref()`.
  - Links, connections and load settings are left out.
  - Failure handling is out of scope: the workflow doesn't stop when a step fails (L4622-4625, L793).
  - The `TRUNCATE` Pre SQLs aren't needed, because tables are rebuilt.
  - The command task is never read; it contains the credential.

  All of these are listed in `flags.md`.
- **The parameter file** (L4554) can override `$$RUN_DATE` in PowerCenter. Here the XML's default is used
  unless you pass `--vars '{run_date: "2025-09-30"}'` to dbt.
- **Anything not in this XML** makes that one model stop at dbt, with the element and its XML line, while
  every other model still converts. `flags.md` lists it under "Not converted", and the command exits with
  code 1 (decision Q18). This covers:
  - other box types (Lookup, Update Strategy, Sequence Generator, Rank, Normalizer, mapplets …);
  - functions the translator doesn't know;
  - expressions that name a missing port;
  - variable ports that read a previous row in any pattern but the counter;
  - Source Qualifier overrides (SQL query, filter, user-defined join, distinct);
  - case-insensitive joins;
  - `DATE_DIFF` in units other than days;
  - mapping variables that aren't parameters.
- **Detail Outer and Full Outer joins** are translated (`right join`, `full join`), but none is in this
  XML, so they are untested.

Step 4 · Translate

Turn each box into SQL with one rule per box type, and turn each port expression into a SQL expression.

One rule per box
Box	Type	Becomes
RAW_ORDERS	PC Source	a table in sources.yml, read with source('raw', 'raw_orders')
SQ_RAW_ORDERS	Source Qualifier	CTE sq_raw_orders: select the 7 columns. No override or filter (L169, L171)
EXP_ORDERS	Expression	CTE exp_orders: one '<expression> as <port>' per output port
SRT_ORDERS	Sorter	dropped with a comment: Distinct is NO (L527) and nothing after it depends on order
STG_ORDERS	PC Target	final select: one column per incoming connector, named after the target column and cast to its type
Port expressions on this path
XML	Informatica	SQL	
L107	ID	sq_raw_orders.id as order_id	pass-through (a rename). Every input is read with its step's name.
L111	SUBTOTAL_IN/100	sq_raw_orders.subtotal / 100 as subtotal	SUBTOTAL_IN is the port fed by SQ_RAW_ORDERS.SUBTOTAL (L647)
L110	TO_DATE(TO_CHAR(ORDERED_AT, 'DD-MM-YY'), 'DD-MM-YY')	strptime(strftime(sq_raw_orders.ordered_at, '%d-%m-%y'), '%d-%m-%y') as ordered_at_day	the same round trip through text (decision Q16). It keeps the day, but the 2-digit year makes DuckDB guess the century back, so it carries a century flag.
Flags in the generated stg_orders.sql (12)
century L110: two-digit year: DuckDB reads 00-68 as 20xx and 69-99 as 19xx; PowerCenter's rule may differ
crossed L608: SRT_ORDERS.SUBTOTAL goes into STG_ORDERS.SUBTOTAL_CENTS, as the connector says
rounds L608: SUBTOTAL is computed as SUBTOTAL_IN/100 (L111), a double at run time because high precision is off, and is rounded to 0 decimal places by the target column SUBTOTAL_CENTS decimal(15,0) (decision Q11)
crossed L609: SRT_ORDERS.TAX_PAID goes into STG_ORDERS.TAX_PAID_CENTS, as the connector says
rounds L609: TAX_PAID is computed as TAX_PAID_IN/100 (L112), a double at run time because high precision is off, and is rounded to 0 decimal places by the target column TAX_PAID_CENTS decimal(15,0) (decision Q11)
crossed L610: SRT_ORDERS.ORDER_TOTAL goes into STG_ORDERS.ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS, as the connector says
rounds L610: ORDER_TOTAL is computed as ORDER_TOTAL_IN/100 (L113), a double at run time because high precision is off, and is rounded to 2 decimal places by the target column ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS decimal(12,2) (decision Q11)
crossed L611: SRT_ORDERS.SUBTOTAL_CENTS goes into STG_ORDERS.SUBTOTAL, as the connector says
rounds L611: SUBTOTAL_CENTS (double) is rounded to 0 decimal places by the target column SUBTOTAL decimal(15,0) (decision Q11)
crossed L612: SRT_ORDERS.TAX_PAID_CENTS goes into STG_ORDERS.TAX_PAID, as the connector says
rounds L612: TAX_PAID_CENTS (double) is rounded to 0 decimal places by the target column TAX_PAID decimal(15,0) (decision Q11)
crossed L613: SRT_ORDERS.ORDER_TOTAL_CENTS goes into STG_ORDERS.ORDER_TOTAL, as the connector says

Watch out

This path needs only 3 kinds of expression. The whole file has 119 logic expressions (IIF, ISNULL, SUM, MAX, ...). That's where most of the translation work was. All of them convert; the Results page shows every box next to its SQL.

RAW_ORDERS	PC Source	a table in sources.yml, read with source('raw', 'raw_orders')

EXP_ORDERS	Expression	CTE exp_orders: one '<expression> as <port>' per output port
SRT_ORDERS	Sorter	dropped with a comment: Distinct is NO (L527) and nothing after it depends on order

XML	Informatica	SQL

## Where the agent got things wrong, and how it was caught

[`agent_log.md`](agent_log.md) lists every mistake, prompt by prompt: what went wrong, who caught it, how,
and what changed. 11 were caught by me and 46 by the agent, which includes two independent
checks it ran in separate agents (prompts 7 and 13). Some that mattered:

- **Said there were 389 expressions to handle;** most are pass-throughs (about 270), and about 120 have real
  logic. Caught by me (prompt 2).
- **Missed that the first-customer flag is always 0,** and that a Master Outer join drops customers.
  Caught by me (prompt 6).
- **Said a whole-number port might round inside the mapping.** With high precision off, it doesn't.
  Caught by me, then checked against Informatica's guides (prompt 8).
- **Said the Union maps ports by position.** It lists field pairs. Caught by the agent while building
  (prompt 9).
- **The SQL relied on DuckDB's rule when a name is both read and written.** Caught by my question; now
  every column carries its step's name (prompt 10).
- **Called the counter's 190 matching rows a coincidence.** They are the first customer's orders. Caught
  by me (prompt 11).
- **Seven rounding flags were missing, and eight seed facts weren't independent of the converter.** Caught
  by the agent's independent check (prompt 13).
- **The seed facts didn't check the margins.** Caught by me (prompt 13).

## Prompts
# pc2dbt: PowerCenter mapping XML to dbt

`pc2dbt` converts an Informatica PowerCenter mapping export (XML) into a dbt project. It was built for the
Infinite Lambda take-home on the demo export `FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml`, and checked against the
dbt-labs jaffle-shop project on the same seed data.

**Results at a glance**

- All 3 mappings convert: 16 dbt models in [`out/`](out/), committed so you can read them without running
  anything, plus [`out/flags.md`](out/flags.md) with 79 flags and 21 left-out items.
- dbt builds all 16 models on DuckDB.
- 133 unit tests and 11 reference tests pass.
- Compared with jaffle-shop: 0 unexplained differences.
- The enriched marts have no jaffle-shop twin, so 21 facts check them, each computed straight from the raw
  seed and all matching.
- The behaviour copied from the XML is listed below and in [`docs/results.html`](docs/results.html).

## How to run

+`pc2dbt` converts an Informatica PowerCenter mapping export (XML) into a dbt project. It was built for the
+Infinite Lambda take-home on the demo export `FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml`, and checked against the

-This README is written in full in build step 4 (how to run, assumptions, what isn't handled, where the

+**Results at a glance**
-## Unknowns
+- All 3 mappings convert: 16 dbt models in [`out/`](out/), committed so you can read them without running
+  anything, plus [`out/flags.md`](out/flags.md) with 79 flags and 21 left-out items.
+- dbt builds all 16 models on DuckDB.
+- 139 unit tests and 12 reference tests pass.
+- Compared with jaffle-shop: 0 unexplained differences.
+- The enriched marts have no jaffle-shop twin, so 21 facts check them, each computed straight from the raw
+  seed and all matching.
+- The behaviour copied from the XML is listed below and in [`docs/results.html`](docs/results.html).
+
+## How to run
+
+You need git, internet access the first time, and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). uv installs Python 3.12
+for you if it isn't there.
+
+```bash
+git clone https://github.com/junaidatique/pc2dbt.git pc2dbt
+cd pc2dbt
+uv venv --python 3.12
+uv pip install -e ".[test]"
+```
+
+Clone the two projects the checks need into `external/` (ignored by git), pinned to the commits used here:
+
+```bash
+git clone https://github.com/infinitelambda/flowline-pwc-demo.git external/flowline-pwc-demo
+git -C external/flowline-pwc-demo checkout 550a222
+git clone https://github.com/dbt-labs/jaffle-shop.git external/jaffle-shop
+git -C external/jaffle-shop checkout 7d0d8de
+```
+
+Convert the XML. This writes the same project that is committed in `out/`, so `git status` shows no change:
+
+```bash
+.venv/bin/pc2dbt convert external/flowline-pwc-demo/FLOWLINE_DEMO_JAFFLESHOP.xml --out out
+git status --short out/
+```
+
+Run the tests. The first command is fast. The second builds both projects with dbt and compares them; the
+first time, it also runs `dbt deps` and builds jaffle-shop (cached in `tests/.cache/`).
+
+```bash
+.venv/bin/pytest
+.venv/bin/pytest -m reference
+```
+
+Build `out/` with dbt yourself. This loads the seed CSVs with the XML's column types, runs `dbt build`, and
+prints the row count of every table. The tables end up in `demo.duckdb`, which you can query:
+
+```bash
+.venv/bin/python tools/build_demo.py
+```
